# 手机部署（Android，实验性）

/zh/docs/guide/deploy/mobile



<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  手机部署是**实验性、进阶**用法，资源消耗大，并不适合大多数人。如果你有一台 PC / 服务器，请优先用 [Docker 部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)。本页只是说明在 Android 上"能跑"的现实路径，并诚实地交代它的限制。
</Callout>

## 现实情况：Docker 在手机上基本跑不动 [#现实情况docker-在手机上基本跑不动]

先把期望摆正：

* **无 root 的 Linux 用户态在 Android 上很容易**——用 Termux + `proot-distro` 装一个 Ubuntu 即可。
* **但真正的 Docker（dockerd）在 proot 下跑不起来。** proot 只是一个基于 ptrace 的系统调用模拟器，没有 namespaces / cgroups / netfilter，而这些正是容器运行时所依赖的。
* 想在手机上跑**真 Docker**只能上虚拟机（Termux 里的 QEMU，或 Podroid 这类 App）。但手机一般没有 KVM，只能走 TCG 软件模拟，**非常慢**，对绝大多数用户不实用。Google AVF 的"Linux 终端"是真 VM，但其官方镜像在 2026 年仍不是开箱即用的容器环境。

**因此手机上的现实推荐：Termux + proot Ubuntu，然后在里面按 [Linux 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/linux-manual) 流程手动跑 SnowLuma。** 手机上的 Docker 留给极客折腾，不在本页推荐范围。

各平台对比见 [部署方式选择](/zh/guide/deploy/)。

## 第一步：装 Termux [#第一步装-termux]

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  **别从 Google Play 装 Termux。** Play 商店里的版本早已停更、有已知问题。请从 **F-Droid** 或 Termux 的 GitHub Releases 安装。
</Callout>

* F-Droid：[https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux/](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux/)
* GitHub：[https://github.com/termux/termux-app/releases](https://github.com/termux/termux-app/releases)

装好后先更新一下：

```bash
pkg update && pkg upgrade
```

## 第二步：装 proot Ubuntu [#第二步装-proot-ubuntu]

```bash
pkg install proot-distro
proot-distro install ubuntu
proot-distro login ubuntu
```

进去之后你就在一个 Ubuntu 用户态里了。文档见 [https://github.com/termux/proot-distro](https://github.com/termux/proot-distro) 与 [https://wiki.termux.com](https://wiki.termux.com)。

## 第三步：在 proot Ubuntu 里跑 Linux 手动流程 [#第三步在-proot-ubuntu-里跑-linux-手动流程]

剩下的步骤和 [Linux 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/linux-manual) **完全一致**，在 proot Ubuntu 里依次做：

1. 安装 Node 24 LTS。
2. 安装 Linux QQ（`.deb`）及 Electron / CJK 依赖（Ubuntu 24.04 注意 `libasound2t64`）。
3. 起 Xvfb + fluxbox + x11vnc + noVNC，用浏览器扫码。
4. 给 node 授予 `cap_sys_ptrace`。
5. 冻结 QQ 热更新（`/etc/hosts` black-hole `qqpatch.gtimg.cn`）。
6. 下载并解包 SnowLuma `-lite` linux tarball，`node ./index.mjs`。
7. 拉起 QQ、扫码、打开 WebUI。

由于一切都在手机本机，noVNC / WebUI 直接用 `http://localhost:6081` / `http://localhost:5099` 在手机浏览器里打开即可。

请直接照搬 [Linux 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/linux-manual) 的完整命令，本页不再重复。

## 诚实的限制说明 [#诚实的限制说明]

* **ptrace 注入在 proot 下可能受限。** SnowLuma 的 hook 靠 ptrace 注入 QQ 进程，而 proot 本身就是个 ptrace 模拟层——两者叠加时注入是否成功**高度取决于设备、内核与 proot 版本**，不保证可用。这是本路径最大的不确定点。
* **资源吃紧。** QQ 是基于 Chromium 的 Electron 应用，外加一整套 Xvfb + VNC + Node，对手机内存 / 发热 / 电量压力很大。低端机基本带不动。
* **arm64。** 手机基本都是 arm64，记得 Node、Linux QQ、SnowLuma 都要选 `arm64` 版本。
* **会话保活。** Termux 进程可能被系统省电策略杀掉；用 Termux 的 wake-lock，并考虑关掉该 App 的电池优化。
* **架构选错就跑不起来。** lite tarball 选 `linux-arm64-lite`，QQ `.deb` 选 arm64。

整体而言：&#x2A;*手机部署可以作为尝鲜 / 应急，但不是稳定生产方案。** 想长期稳定，请用 PC / 服务器上的 [Docker 部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)。

## 关于"手机上的 Docker" [#关于手机上的-docker]

如果你执意要在手机上跑 Docker，唯一可行方向是在 Termux 里用 QEMU 起一个 x86\_64/arm64 的 Linux 虚拟机、在 VM 里装真 Docker，再按 [Docker 部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker) 操作。但没有 KVM 的纯软件模拟非常慢，**不推荐**，这里仅作说明，不展开。

## 相关链接 [#相关链接]

* [部署方式选择](/zh/guide/deploy/)
* [Linux 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/linux-manual) — 本页的核心步骤都在这里
* [Docker 部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker) — 真正推荐的方式
* [配置说明](/zh/guide/configuration)


---

# Docker 持久化数据迁移

/zh/docs/guide/deploy/storage-migration



新版本统一了容器内的持久化布局。Docker 不会自动把已有命名卷的数据复制到新的命名卷，因此，从旧版 Docker 配置升级时需要迁移一次。

迁移会保留 SnowLuma 配置、OneBot 配置、QQ 登录状态和 QQ 本地数据。整个过程不会删除旧数据卷。

<Callout type="error" title="开始前">
  * 保留旧容器，先不要执行 `docker compose down` 或删除容器。
  * 不要执行 `docker compose down -v`，它会删除 Compose 管理的数据卷。
  * 迁移时需要停止容器，请预留短暂停机时间。
  * 宿主机应留有足够空间，迁移期间新旧数据会同时存在。
</Callout>

## 1. 确认旧容器 [#1-确认旧容器]

以下命令默认容器名是 `snowluma`。如果你修改过容器名，请替换第一行。

```bash
CONTAINER=snowluma
docker inspect "$CONTAINER" >/dev/null
docker inspect "$CONTAINER" \
  --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{printf "%-24s %-8s %s\n" .Destination .Type .Name}}{{end}}'
```

输出中应能看到以下三个容器路径：

```text
/app/snowluma-data
/app/.config
/app/.local/share
```

如果缺少任一路径，请停止迁移并检查原部署配置。

## 2. 停止容器 [#2-停止容器]

停止容器可以避免配置数据库或 QQ 登录数据在复制过程中继续变化。

```bash
docker stop "$CONTAINER"
```

不要删除这个容器。后续复制会直接读取它当前挂载的数据，因此不需要猜测 Compose 自动生成的卷名。

## 3. 创建当前数据卷 [#3-创建当前数据卷]

```bash
docker volume create qq-gateway-data
docker volume create qq-client-config
docker volume create qq-client-data
```

确认三个目标卷都是空的：

```bash
docker run --rm \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/check/gateway \
  -v qq-client-config:/check/config \
  -v qq-client-data:/check/share \
  alpine:3.21 sh -ec '
    for path in /check/gateway /check/config /check/share; do
      [ -z "$(ls -A "$path")" ] || {
        echo "目标数据卷不是空的：$path" >&2
        exit 1
      }
    done
  '
```

如果这里报错，请不要覆盖目标卷。先确认它是否来自之前未完成的迁移。

## 4. 复制并校验数据 [#4-复制并校验数据]

下面的命令以只读方式挂载旧容器的数据卷，将数据复制到当前数据卷，并逐文件校验内容。首次运行可能需要下载体积较小的 `alpine` 镜像。

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --volumes-from "${CONTAINER}:ro" \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/migration/gateway \
  -v qq-client-config:/migration/config \
  -v qq-client-data:/migration/share \
  alpine:3.21 sh -ec '
    copy_tree() {
      source_path="$1"
      target_path="$2"
      label="$3"

      [ -d "$source_path" ] || {
        echo "缺少源目录：$source_path" >&2
        exit 1
      }

      (cd "$source_path" && tar -cf - .) |
        (cd "$target_path" && tar -xpf -)

      (cd "$source_path" && find . -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; | sort) > "/tmp/${label}.source"
      (cd "$target_path" && find . -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; | sort) > "/tmp/${label}.target"
      cmp "/tmp/${label}.source" "/tmp/${label}.target"
      echo "已校验：$label"
    }

    copy_tree /app/snowluma-data /migration/gateway gateway
    copy_tree /app/.config /migration/config config
    copy_tree /app/.local/share /migration/share share
  '
```

命令应依次输出：

```text
已校验：gateway
已校验：config
已校验：share
```

任何一步失败都应停止迁移，不要继续启动新配置。旧数据仍保留在原数据卷中。

## 5. 更新 Compose 配置 [#5-更新-compose-配置]

将服务的数据卷挂载改为：

```yaml
services:
  snowluma:
    volumes:
      - qq-gateway-data:/app/data
      - qq-client-config:/app/.config
      - qq-client-data:/app/.local/share

volumes:
  qq-gateway-data:
    name: qq-gateway-data
  qq-client-config:
    name: qq-client-config
  qq-client-data:
    name: qq-client-data
```

然后拉取并启动当前镜像：

```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

如果使用 `docker run`，先删除已停止的旧容器，再用相同端口和环境变量重新创建容器，并使用下面三个挂载：

```bash
-v qq-gateway-data:/app/data \
-v qq-client-config:/app/.config \
-v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share
```

## 6. 验证迁移结果 [#6-验证迁移结果]

迁移完成后依次确认：

1. 容器保持运行，日志中没有持续出现启动错误。
2. WebUI 可以使用原凭据登录，原有设置仍然存在。
3. QQ 保持原登录状态，不需要重新扫码。
4. OneBot 的监听端、令牌和机器人连接均与迁移前一致。
5. 实际收发一条测试消息，确认事件接收和消息发送正常。

```bash
docker ps --filter "name=${CONTAINER}"
docker logs --tail 100 "$CONTAINER"
```

<Callout type="idea" title="保留回滚能力">
  确认服务稳定前，请保留旧容器配置和旧数据卷。需要回滚时，停止当前容器，恢复升级前的 Compose 文件和镜像版本，再重新启动即可。

  旧数据卷不会被本流程自动删除。建议至少完成一次容器重启并再次确认登录状态后，再自行决定是否清理。
</Callout>

## 绑定目录与多账号 [#绑定目录与多账号]

### 使用宿主机目录 [#使用宿主机目录]

如果第一步显示挂载类型为 `bind`，数据已经位于宿主机目录，不需要复制 Docker 命名卷。保留原宿主机目录，只将应用数据的容器目标从 `/app/snowluma-data` 改为 `/app/data`；QQ 的两个目标路径保持不变。

### 多账号 [#多账号]

额外 QQ 账号的挂载路径仍是 `/app/qq-acct2`、`/app/qq-acct3` 等。如果希望同时更换这些命名卷，请为每个账号创建独立的新卷，重复第四步的复制与校验流程，并确保一个账号只挂载一个独立的完整 `HOME`。


---

# 更新

/zh/docs/guide/deploy/update



升级 SnowLuma 的核心原则只有一条：**只替换程序，不动数据**。登录态、账号配置、运行时配置都在数据目录 / 数据卷里，升级时保留它们就不用重新扫码、不用重配。

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  WebUI 会提示有新版本可用，可以据此决定何时升级。
</Callout>

## Docker [#docker]

最简单。用 Compose：

```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

或者手动拉镜像后重建容器：

```bash
docker pull motricseven7/snowluma:latest
docker stop snowluma && docker rm snowluma
# 用和原来完全相同的 docker run 命令重新创建（卷不变）
```

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  **不要删除数据卷**（`qq-gateway-data`、`qq-client-config`、`qq-client-data`）。删了就会丢登录态和配置。`docker rm` 只删容器、不删卷，重建时挂上同名卷即可无缝衔接。
</Callout>

## 手动 tarball [#手动-tarball]

1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/releases) 下载新版本对应平台 / 架构的 tarball（full 或 lite，和你原来用的保持一致）。
2. 替换程序文件（`index.mjs`、`webui/`、`native/` 等），**保留你的配置 / 数据目录**（`config/` 及其同级数据）。
3. 重新启动：`node ./index.mjs`（Windows 上也可双击 `launcher.bat`）。

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  建议把数据目录放在解包目录之外，或升级前先备份它，这样直接整目录替换也不会误删配置。
</Callout>

## 从源码构建 [#从源码构建]

```bash
git pull
pnpm install
pnpm build:all
```

`dist/` 会重新生成（`index.mjs`、`launcher.bat`、`webui/`、`native/`）。同样**不要动**你的数据目录，重启即可。

## 版本固定与 QQ 版本 [#版本固定与-qq-版本]

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  内置的 QQ 版本与 native hook &#x2A;*绑定（pinned）**。升级 SnowLuma 本身是安全的，但**不要手动升级容器 / 环境里的那个 QQ**——QQ 的版本一旦变了，版本绑定的 native hook 可能就失效了。

  Docker 镜像已经通过把 QQ 的静默热更新主机黑洞掉来冻结 QQ 版本（详见 [Linux 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/linux-manual)）。手动 / 非 Docker 环境也应自行阻止 QQ 自动更新。
</Callout>

生产环境建议固定具体的镜像 / 发行版本 tag（例如 `motricseven7/snowluma:v1.10.0`），而不是一直用 `:latest`，这样升级是显式、可控、可回滚的。


---

# Windows · Docker Desktop

/zh/docs/guide/deploy/windows-docker



<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  **先说清楚：SnowLuma 的 Docker 镜像是 Linux 的。** 它在容器里跑的是**无头 Linux QQ** + Xvfb + VNC + noVNC。在 Windows 上你是通过 Docker Desktop 的 **WSL2 后端**来运行这个 Linux 容器——本质上还是在一个轻量 Linux 虚拟机里跑。
</Callout>

如果你想在 Windows 上跑**原生 Windows QQ**（`QQ.exe`），那不该用 Docker，请走 [Windows 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/windows)。本页讲的是“我就想用容器、不想碰原生 QQ”的场景。

启动后的容器和 [Docker（Linux）部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)**完全一样**——同一个镜像、同样的 `docker run` / Compose、同样的端口。本页只补上 Windows 这一侧的前置准备。

## 安装 Docker Desktop [#安装-docker-desktop]

到 [docs.docker.com](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install/) 下载 `Docker Desktop Installer.exe`，用**默认的 WSL2 后端**安装。

### 系统要求 [#系统要求]

* Windows 10 22H2 或 Windows 11 23H2 及以上
* WSL ≥ 2.1.5
* 8 GB 内存
* BIOS 里开启虚拟化（VT-x / AMD-V），以及 SLAT

安装时如果勾选了 WSL2 后端（默认），Docker Desktop 会自动帮你装 / 启用 WSL2。装完重启，启动 Docker Desktop。

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  确认用的是 WSL2 后端而不是旧的 Hyper-V 后端：Docker Desktop → Settings → General → 勾选 **Use the WSL 2 based engine**。
</Callout>

如果你想自己装 / 管理 WSL2（或在 WSL 发行版里直接装原生 Docker Engine，而不走 Docker Desktop），见 [WSL2](/zh/guide/deploy/wsl2)。

## 运行 SnowLuma 容器 [#运行-snowluma-容器]

Docker Desktop 就绪后，直接用[规范 Docker 页](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)里的同一条命令。打开 PowerShell：

```powershell
docker run -d `
  --name snowluma `
  --restart unless-stopped `
  --shm-size=1g `
  --ulimit nofile=65536:1048576 `
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE `
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined `
  -p 6081:6081 `
  -p 5099:5099 `
  -p 3000:3000 `
  -p 3001:3001 `
  -v qq-gateway-data:/app/data `
  -v qq-client-config:/app/.config `
  -v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share `
  motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` 和 `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` **仍然不能省**。SnowLuma 的 native addon 通过 ptrace 把 hook 注入容器内的 QQ 进程，默认 seccomp profile 会拦截。Docker Desktop 的 WSL2 后端会把这两项透传进 WSL2 内核，所以照常工作。
</Callout>

Compose、环境变量、数据卷、多账号等完整参考**不在这里重复**——一切都和 Linux 上一致，请直接看 [Docker（Linux）部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)。Compose 在 PowerShell 里同样可用：

```powershell
docker compose up -d
```

## 访问 [#访问]

容器内服务通过 `localhost` 直接访问（Docker Desktop 把端口转发到 Windows 主机）：

| 地址                       | 用途                       |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ |
| `http://localhost:6081/` | noVNC——浏览器里看远程桌面、扫码登录 QQ |
| `http://localhost:5099/` | SnowLuma WebUI           |
| `http://localhost:3000/` | OneBot HTTP              |
| `ws://localhost:3001/`   | OneBot WebSocket         |

首次登录流程（noVNC 扫码、找 WebUI 临时密码等）和 Linux 一模一样，见 [Docker（Linux）部署 · 首次登录](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)。

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  远程桌面**没有**固定默认密码：第一次启动会随机生成，只在容器日志里打印一次。不要把 noVNC / WebUI / OneBot 端口裸暴露到公网。完整说明见 [Docker 部署 · 远程桌面密码](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)。
</Callout>

## 该看哪一页 [#该看哪一页]

* [Docker（Linux）部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker) —— 镜像、端口、Compose、环境变量、数据卷、多账号的**完整参考**。本页只是 Windows 前置。
* [WSL2](/zh/guide/deploy/wsl2) —— 不想用 Docker Desktop？可以在 WSL 发行版里装原生 Docker Engine 跑同一个容器。
* [Windows 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/windows) —— 想跑原生 Windows QQ（`QQ.exe`）而不是容器里的 Linux QQ。


---

# Windows 手动部署

/zh/docs/guide/deploy/windows



在 Windows 上 SnowLuma **原生运行**，不需要 Docker、不需要 WSL2。你只要装好桌面版 QQ，下载对应的 SnowLuma 发行包解压，运行即可——SnowLuma 会自动发现 `QQ.exe` 并注入 hook。

> 想用容器跑？见 [Windows · Docker Desktop](/zh/guide/deploy/windows-docker)（注意：镜像是 Linux 的，跑的是 Linux QQ）。

## 准备工作 [#准备工作]

### 1. 安装桌面版 QQ（NTQQ） [#1-安装桌面版-qqntqq]

从腾讯官网下载并安装 Windows 桌面版 QQ（NT 架构），装好后能正常打开 `QQ.exe`。SnowLuma 注入的是这个正在运行的 NTQQ 进程。

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  版本匹配很重要。SnowLuma 的 native hook 是按 QQ 版本对齐的。如果 QQ 自动升到了一个 SnowLuma 还不支持的新版本，hook 可能加载失败——遇到问题先看 WebUI / README 里的版本兼容说明。
</Callout>

### 2. 下载 SnowLuma 发行包 [#2-下载-snowluma-发行包]

到 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/releases) 选 `win-x64`，两种风味二选一：

| 包                                    | 说明                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `SnowLuma-<TAG>-win-x64.tar.gz`      | **完整版**，内置 Node.js 运行时，不用单独装 Node，包体较大。 |
| `SnowLuma-<TAG>-win-x64-lite.tar.gz` | **精简版**，不含 Node.js，需要你自己先装好 Node，体积小很多。 |

把 `<TAG>` 换成你要的版本号（例如 `v1.10.0`）。

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  不想折腾就选**完整版**，自带 Node，解压即用。
</Callout>

### 3.（仅精简版）安装 Node.js [#3仅精简版安装-nodejs]

SnowLuma 需要 **Node.js ≥ 22**。截至 2026 年，**Node 24（“Krypton”）是 Active LTS**，22（“Jod”）是 Maintenance LTS。精简版请安装 **Node 24 LTS**（22 也能跑）。

到 [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases) 下载 Windows 安装包，装完用 PowerShell 验证：

```powershell
node -v
# 应输出 v24.x.x（或 v22.x.x）
```

完整版自带运行时，**跳过这一步**。

## 解压并运行 [#解压并运行]

把下载的 tarball 解压到一个固定目录，例如 `C:\SnowLuma\`。解压后目录里有 `index.mjs`、`launcher.bat`、`webui/`、`native/` 等。

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  `.tar.gz` 可以用 Windows 自带的 `tar`（Win10/11 已内置）解压：

  ```powershell
  tar -xzf SnowLuma-<TAG>-win-x64.tar.gz -C C:\SnowLuma
  ```

  也可以用 7-Zip 等工具。
</Callout>

进入解压目录后，双击 `launcher.bat` 启动（它本质就是跑 `node ./index.mjs` 再 `pause`，方便你看输出）。或者在终端里手动跑：

```powershell
cd C:\SnowLuma
node ./index.mjs
```

完整版若用了内置 Node，请按 README 指引启动（一般直接 `launcher.bat` 即可）；具体见 WebUI / README。

## QQ 与 SnowLuma 的启动顺序 [#qq-与-snowluma-的启动顺序]

SnowLuma 默认开启 **hook 自动加载**：它会持续探测系统里的 QQ 主进程，发现 `QQ.exe` 就自动把 hook 注入进去（先进入被动观察），等你扫码登录完成后，hook 自动从被动观察切到工作模式。

所以两种顺序都行：

* **先开 QQ 再开 SnowLuma**：SnowLuma 启动后立刻发现已在运行的 `QQ.exe` 并注入。
* **先开 SnowLuma 再开 QQ**：SnowLuma 会等到 `QQ.exe` 出现后再注入。

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  **必须用和 QQ 相同的 Windows 用户运行 SnowLuma。** 注入需要能访问目标进程；如果 SnowLuma 和 QQ 跑在不同用户（或权限不对等）下，注入会失败。如果一个以管理员身份运行、另一个没有，也可能注入不上——保持二者权限一致。
</Callout>

### 登录 [#登录]

登录**只支持扫码**：在桌面上打开的 QQ 窗口里用手机 QQ 扫码登录。原生 Windows 上你本来就能看到 QQ 窗口，不需要 VNC/noVNC（那是 Linux 无头环境才用的）。

### 关闭自动注入（可选） [#关闭自动注入可选]

想保留传统的“WebUI 里手动 Load”流程，把 `runtime.json` 里的 `hookAutoLoad` 设为 `false`，或设环境变量 `SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD=0`。环境变量优先。

## 访问 WebUI 和 OneBot [#访问-webui-和-onebot]

启动后，默认监听这些端口：

| 端口     | 用途                   |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| `5099` | SnowLuma WebUI       |
| `3000` | OneBot HTTP（默认）      |
| `3001` | OneBot WebSocket（默认） |

浏览器打开 WebUI：

```text
http://127.0.0.1:5099/
```

### 找 WebUI 临时密码 [#找-webui-临时密码]

**全新数据目录首次启动**时，会在控制台 / 日志里输出一次性管理员密码。从 `launcher.bat` 弹出的控制台窗口里翻一下即可（找含“临时密码 / initial credentials”的那行）。

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  临时密码**只在全新数据目录首次启动时**输出一次，复用旧目录或重启都不会重新生成。具体提示文案见 WebUI / README。
</Callout>

## 配置文件落在哪 [#配置文件落在哪]

首次运行会在数据目录下自动创建配置：

| 文件                         | 作用                                  |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `config/onebot.json`       | 全局默认 OneBot 配置。                     |
| `config/onebot_<uin>.json` | 每个账号一份（按 UIN）。                      |
| `config/runtime.json`      | WebUI 端口、`hookAutoLoad`、日志级别等运行时设置。 |

环境变量优先级高于 `runtime.json`。多账号无需手动配置：每登录一个 UIN，SnowLuma 自动拉起一个 OneBot 实例。配置项详解见 [配置参考](/zh/guide/configuration)。

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  数据目录的确切位置见 WebUI / README（不同打包方式可能不同）。
</Callout>

## 防火墙 [#防火墙]

首次启动时，Windows 防火墙可能弹窗询问是否放行 `node` / SnowLuma 的网络访问。

* 只在**本机**访问（`127.0.0.1`）时，可以不放行公网。
* 想让局域网内其它设备访问 WebUI / OneBot，需要在防火墙放行对应端口（`5099` / `3000` / `3001`）。

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  **不要把 WebUI / OneBot 端口裸暴露到公网。** 这些端口能完全控制你的 QQ。如需远程访问，请走反向代理 + 鉴权或内网穿透 + 鉴权，并改掉默认凭据。
</Callout>

## 下一步 [#下一步]

* [配置参考](/zh/guide/configuration) —— OneBot / runtime 配置项详解。
* [快速开始](/zh/guide/quickstart) —— 连接你的第一个 OneBot 客户端。
* [MCP 使用](/zh/mcp/) / [SDK](/zh/sdk/) —— 二次开发。
* 其它平台：[Docker（Linux）](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)、[WSL2](/zh/guide/deploy/wsl2)、[部署方式总览](/zh/guide/deploy/)。


---

# WSL2

/zh/docs/guide/deploy/wsl2



WSL2（Windows Subsystem for Linux 2）在 Windows 上提供一个真正的 Linux 内核。在它里面跑 SnowLuma 的 Linux 容器，是不想用原生 Windows QQ 时的另一条路。

本页讲：先装好 WSL2，再用两种方式之一把 Docker 跑起来，最后启动[规范的 SnowLuma 容器](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)。

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  如果你已经在用 / 打算用 **Docker Desktop**，它自带 WSL2 集成，更省事——直接看 [Windows · Docker Desktop](/zh/guide/deploy/windows-docker)。本页适合想在 WSL 发行版里**自己装 Docker Engine**、或想更贴近 Linux 操作的人。
</Callout>

## 1. 安装 WSL2 [#1-安装-wsl2]

以**管理员**身份打开 PowerShell，运行：

```powershell
wsl --install
```

这会装好 WSL2 + 默认的 Ubuntu 发行版。**重启**电脑，重启后 Ubuntu 会首次启动，让你创建 Linux 用户名和密码。

确认版本是 2：

```powershell
wsl -l -v
# VERSION 一列应为 2
wsl --set-default-version 2
```

当前 Ubuntu-on-WSL 默认已开启 systemd。

> 官方文档：[https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install)

## 2. 在 WSL2 里准备 Docker（二选一，别两个都装） [#2-在-wsl2-里准备-docker二选一别两个都装]

### 方式 A：Docker Desktop 的 WSL 集成（推荐） [#方式-adocker-desktop-的-wsl-集成推荐]

装好 Docker Desktop 后，到 Settings → Resources → WSL Integration，给你的 Ubuntu 发行版打开集成开关。这样在 Ubuntu 终端里就能直接用 `docker` 命令，引擎跑在 Docker Desktop 那边。安装与系统要求见 [Windows · Docker Desktop](/zh/guide/deploy/windows-docker)。

> 官方文档：[https://docs.docker.com/desktop/features/wsl/](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/features/wsl/)

### 方式 B：发行版内的原生 Docker Engine [#方式-b发行版内的原生-docker-engine]

不想装 Docker Desktop，就在 Ubuntu 发行版里直接装原生 Docker Engine。官方 apt 仓库（deb822 `docker.sources` 格式）方式见 [https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/)。

仅用于本机 / 开发，也可以用便捷脚本：

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
```

加完用户组要**重开终端**才生效。启动 Docker：

```bash
# 已开 systemd 的发行版：
sudo systemctl start docker
sudo systemctl enable docker

# 没开 systemd 的旧环境：
sudo service docker start
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  **A、B 二选一，不要两个都装。** Docker Desktop 集成和发行版内的原生 dockerd 同时存在会互相打架。
</Callout>

## 3. 运行 SnowLuma 容器 [#3-运行-snowluma-容器]

Docker 就绪后，在 Ubuntu 终端里运行和[规范 Docker 页](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)完全一样的命令：

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name snowluma \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --shm-size=1g \
  --ulimit nofile=65536:1048576 \
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  -p 6081:6081 \
  -p 5099:5099 \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -p 3001:3001 \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/app/data \
  -v qq-client-config:/app/.config \
  -v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share \
  motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` 和 `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` **不能省**——hook 通过 ptrace 注入，默认 seccomp 会拦。
</Callout>

Compose、环境变量、数据卷、多账号、首次登录等**完整参考都在** [Docker（Linux）部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)，本页不重复。

## 4. 从 Windows 访问端口 [#4-从-windows-访问端口]

WSL2 默认会把容器监听的端口转发到 Windows 的 `localhost`，所以在 Windows 浏览器里直接用 `localhost` 即可：

| 地址                       | 用途               |
| ------------------------ | ---------------- |
| `http://localhost:6081/` | noVNC（扫码登录 QQ）   |
| `http://localhost:5099/` | SnowLuma WebUI   |
| `http://localhost:3000/` | OneBot HTTP      |
| `ws://localhost:3001/`   | OneBot WebSocket |

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  极少数环境下 `localhost` 转发可能失效（被关闭或网络模式不同）。这时用 `wsl hostname -I` 拿到 WSL 的 IP，再用那个 IP 访问。
</Callout>

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  远程桌面**没有**固定默认密码：第一次启动会随机生成，只在容器日志里打印一次。不要把 noVNC / WebUI / OneBot 端口裸暴露到公网。完整说明见 [Docker 部署 · 远程桌面密码](/zh/guide/deploy/docker)。
</Callout>

## 也可以：在 WSL2 里走 Linux 手动流程 [#也可以在-wsl2-里走-linux-手动流程]

WSL2 终究是个 Linux 环境，理论上你也能在里面不靠 Docker、直接按 Linux 手动方式跑 SnowLuma（自己起 Xvfb / VNC / noVNC、装 linuxqq、给 node 加 ptrace capability 等）。但那套步骤明显更繁琐，**Docker 更省事**，所以本页推荐容器路线。

## 该看哪一页 [#该看哪一页]

* [Docker（Linux）部署](/zh/guide/deploy/docker) —— 容器的完整参考。
* [Windows · Docker Desktop](/zh/guide/deploy/windows-docker) —— 用 Docker Desktop 而不是发行版内 Engine。
* [Windows 手动部署](/zh/guide/deploy/windows) —— 想跑原生 Windows QQ 而不是容器里的 Linux QQ。


---

# API reference

/en/docs/api



SnowLuma's HTTP API is OneBot v11 compatible. Each action is one page, rendered by the OpenAPI plugin: request body, auth, the response envelope, code samples, and a try-it panel against your own instance.

## Calling it [#calling-it]

* Method: `POST /{action}`
* Body: `Content-Type: application/json`
* Default server: `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` (on the same Docker network: `http://snowluma:3000/`)
* Auth (when a token is configured): `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or `?access_token=`
* WebSocket: `ws://127.0.0.1:3001/`, same action names as HTTP

## Response envelope [#response-envelope]

HTTP 200 can still be a business failure. Read `retcode`:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "retcode": 0,
  "data": {},
  "message": "",
  "wording": ""
}
```

Success is `retcode` `0`. The shape of `data` is on each action page.

## Try it from the docs [#try-it-from-the-docs]

Open any action page, set the server URL and token, and send from the try-it panel. The browser talks to the server you entered, not to this documentation site.

MCP clients do not need handwritten HTTP. See [MCP](/docs/mcp).

## All actions [#all-actions]

<ApiCatalog lang="en" />

# Networks in China

/en/docs/guide/china-network



The installer already treats failures per hop: it names the hop that failed and the next action. You can do the same by hand.

## Docker images [#docker-images]

Official image: `motricseven7/snowluma`.

If Hub times out or rate-limits, pull through a prefix and retag:

```bash
docker pull docker.1ms.run/motricseven7/snowluma:latest
docker tag docker.1ms.run/motricseven7/snowluma:latest motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

`docker.xuanyuan.me/` and `docker.m.daocloud.io/` are other public prefixes. They churn; do not treat any one of them as the only source.

On cloud VMs prefer the vendor's registry mirror. On **1Panel / Baota**, set it in the panel. Do not let a script rewrite `daemon.json`.

## Installing Docker Engine [#installing-docker-engine]

Do not pipe random Gitee installers.

* Ubuntu/Debian: Aliyun / Tsinghua `docker-ce` mirrors
* The installer uses those, then `get.docker.com --mirror Aliyun`
* OpenCloudOS / openEuler: do not use the distro's ancient `docker` package

## Installer script [#installer-script]

If `raw.githubusercontent.com` is blocked in the one-liner:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ghfast.top/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh | bash
```

Templates then come from jsDelivr / ghfast. Do not swap in a random Gitee installer.

## GitHub releases (lite tarball, host mode) [#github-releases-lite-tarball-host-mode]

`github.com` / `objects.githubusercontent.com` can stall. The host-mode installer tries ghfast, gh-proxy, then GitHub, and verifies checksums when they exist.

Do not put GitHub reverse proxies into Docker `registry-mirrors`.

## Linux QQ packages [#linux-qq-packages]

Use Tencent's CDN `qqdl.gtimg.cn`. The image build pins the current official filename plus a pinned backup; it never follows `latest`.


---

# Configuration

/en/docs/guide/configuration



SnowLuma stores configuration in two JSON files:

* **`config/onebot.json` + `config/onebot_<uin>.json`** — OneBot network adapters (HTTP/WebSocket listeners, reverse WS, HTTP event reporting).
* **`config/runtime.json`** — process-level settings (WebUI port, auto-injection toggle).

Both files are auto-generated on first run and normalized on every load.

## OneBot config [#onebot-config]

### File locations [#file-locations]

```text
config/onebot.json          # global defaults
config/onebot_<uin>.json    # per-account overrides
```

* **Global**: `config/onebot.json` — the default for every account.
* **Per-account**: `config/onebot_<uin>.json` — overrides the global file.
* **Auto-generated**: missing per-account config or access tokens are written automatically in normalized form on first run.

### Default config [#default-config]

Adapters are grouped by kind under a single `networks` object:

```json
{
  "networks": {
    "httpServers": [
      {
        "name": "http-default",
        "enabled": true,
        "host": "0.0.0.0",
        "port": 3000,
        "path": "/",
        "accessToken": "auto-generated",
        "messageFormat": "array",
        "reportSelfMessage": false
      }
    ],
    "httpClients": [],
    "wsServers": [
      {
        "name": "ws-default",
        "enabled": true,
        "host": "0.0.0.0",
        "port": 3001,
        "path": "/",
        "role": "Universal",
        "accessToken": "auto-generated",
        "messageFormat": "array",
        "reportSelfMessage": false
      }
    ],
    "wsClients": []
  },
  "musicSignUrl": ""
}
```

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  **Migrating from the old format**: earlier versions kept `httpServers` / `wsServers` arrays at the top level and used `httpPostEndpoints` for reporting. SnowLuma detects this layout, moves the entries into the `networks` object, renames `httpPostEndpoints` to `httpClients`, and writes the result back to disk. If you maintain configs by hand, use the new shape.
</Callout>

### Shared fields [#shared-fields]

Every adapter accepts these (`NetworkBase`):

| Field               | Type   | Default  | Notes                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`              | string | required | Identifier unique within its kind array; hot-reload addresses it by `(kind, name)`.                        |
| `enabled`           | bool   | `true`   | Set `false` to keep the configuration but skip starting this adapter.                                      |
| `accessToken`       | string | auto     | OneBot bearer / `?access_token=`.                                                                          |
| `messageFormat`     | string | `array`  | `array` or `string` — controls whether the event `message` field is a segment array or a flattened string. |
| `reportSelfMessage` | bool   | `false`  | When `true`, this adapter sees `post_type='message_sent'` events.                                          |

### `httpServers` [#httpservers]

OneBot HTTP API listener.

| Field  | Type   | Default   | Notes            |
| ------ | ------ | --------- | ---------------- |
| `host` | string | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address.    |
| `port` | number | `3000`    | Listen port.     |
| `path` | string | `/`       | API path prefix. |

### `httpClients` [#httpclients]

Push events to external endpoints (formerly `httpPostEndpoints`).

| Field       | Type   | Default  | Notes            |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------- |
| `url`       | string | required | Report URL.      |
| `timeoutMs` | number | `5000`   | Request timeout. |

### `wsServers` [#wsservers]

OneBot WebSocket server.

| Field  | Type   | Default     | Notes                                                                                          |
| ------ | ------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host` | string | `0.0.0.0`   | Bind address.                                                                                  |
| `port` | number | `3001`      | Listen port.                                                                                   |
| `path` | string | `/`         | WebSocket path.                                                                                |
| `role` | string | `Universal` | `Api`, `Event`, or `Universal` (**TitleCase**; older lowercase values are no longer accepted). |

### `wsClients` [#wsclients]

Connect outbound to reverse WebSocket servers.

| Field                 | Type   | Default     | Notes                                            |
| --------------------- | ------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `url`                 | string | required    | Reverse WebSocket URL.                           |
| `role`                | string | `Universal` | Same values as `wsServers.role`.                 |
| `reconnectIntervalMs` | number | `5000`      | Reconnect interval; clamped to a `1000` minimum. |

### `musicSignUrl` [#musicsignurl]

Optional URL for a custom music-card signing service. Empty string disables.

## Runtime config (`runtime.json`) [#runtime-config-runtimejson]

`config/runtime.json` carries process-wide settings — **not per-account**.

```json
{
  "webuiPort": 5099,
  "hookAutoLoad": false
}
```

| Field          | Type   | Default | Notes                                                                                        |
| -------------- | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `webuiPort`    | number | `5099`  | WebUI listen port; out-of-range values fall back to the default.                             |
| `hookAutoLoad` | bool   | `false` | Auto-inject the hook into every newly discovered QQ process. The Docker image flips this on. |

## Environment variables [#environment-variables]

| Var                         | Notes                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD`    | `1` / `true` forces auto-injection on; `0` / `false` off. &#x2A;*Wins over `runtime.json`**, which makes Docker overrides ergonomic. |
| `SNOWLUMA_LOG_LEVEL`        | Log level (`error` / `warn` / `info` / `debug`).                                                                                     |
| `SNOWLUMA_VERBOSE_WARMUP=1` | Verbose friend / group / member warm-up logs.                                                                                        |
| `SNOWLUMA_DEV_MODE=1`       | Enable dev mode (relaxes WebUI auth for local debugging).                                                                            |
| `SNOWLUMA_DEV_WEBUI=1`      | Force-start the bundled WebUI under dev mode.                                                                                        |

## Port conflicts [#port-conflicts]

If `3000` / `3001` / `5099` are taken, change the matching `port` / `webuiPort` and restart. Docker users can also remap host ports via Compose (see [Docker deployment](/docs/guide/deploy/docker)).


---

# Connect a bot

/en/docs/guide/connect-bot



SnowLuma is a protocol layer, not a bot framework. The bot process connects to it.

In the Docker image, OneBot listens on `0.0.0.0` so sibling containers on the same network can reach it. Non-Docker installs still default to loopback.

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `?access_token=`. Tokens live in the WebUI or `config/onebot.json` / `onebot_<uin>.json`. HTTP and WS tokens can differ.

## Forward: the bot dials SnowLuma [#forward-the-bot-dials-snowluma]

This is what **MaiBot** expects (its SnowLuma / NapCat adapter is a client).

|           |                         |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| HTTP API  | `http://snowluma:3000/` |
| WebSocket | `ws://snowluma:3001/`   |

Inside a bot container use the Docker DNS name `snowluma`, not `127.0.0.1`.

Clients on the host can use `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` when the port is published.

## Reverse: SnowLuma dials the bot [#reverse-snowluma-dials-the-bot]

This is what **AstrBot** and **NoneBot2** expect. Add a `wsClients` entry in SnowLuma (WebUI: reverse WebSocket):

| Framework | Typical URL                       |
| --------- | --------------------------------- |
| AstrBot   | `ws://astrbot:6199/ws`            |
| NoneBot2  | `ws://nonebot:8080/onebot/v11/ws` |

Trust the bot's own docs for the path. SnowLuma only dials out.

HTTP event POST uses `httpClients` with the bot's webhook URL.

## Sidecar install [#sidecar-install]

If you already have a MaiBot / AstrBot compose stack:

```bash
./install.sh --mode compose --network maim_bot --yes
```

Replace `maim_bot` with the real name from `docker network ls`. The installer **does not edit** the other project's files.

Then point the bot adapter at `snowluma:3001` (forward) or fill in the reverse URL on the SnowLuma side.

## Multiple accounts [#multiple-accounts]

Each UIN has `onebot_<uin>.json`. Defaults all want `3000` / `3001`; a second account needs other ports, or reverse WS to distinct bot endpoints.

Full field list: [Configuration](/docs/guide/configuration).


---

# Developer guide

/en/docs/guide/developer



SnowLuma is a TypeScript + native-module hybrid. TypeScript handles runtime orchestration, the OneBot implementation, the protocol bridge, the SDK, and the WebUI; native modules cover the hook, injection, and the high-performance WebSocket implementation.

## Monorepo layout [#monorepo-layout]

pnpm workspace with five packages:

```text
SnowLuma/
├─ packages/
│  ├─ core/        @snowluma/core       Bridge / OneBot / Hook orchestration
│  ├─ websocket/   @snowluma/websocket  In-tree WS impl (uses native addon)
│  ├─ sdk/         @snowluma/sdk        Typed OneBot client for external use
│  ├─ webui/       webui                React + Vite console
│  └─ runtime/     distribution templates (launcher, package.json, scripts)
├─ native/         per-platform native artefacts (.node / .dll / .so)
├─ dist/           build output
├─ tools/          helper scripts (version bump, release, etc.)
├─ docs/           ADRs and developer notes
└─ package.json
```

## Core startup chain [#core-startup-chain]

Entry point: [`packages/core/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/blob/main/packages/core/src/index.ts).

```text
loadRuntimeConfig()           ← reads config/runtime.json / env
  ↓
HookManager(autoLoadOnDiscovery)
  ↓
BridgeManager
  ↓
OneBotManager                 ← spins up OneBotInstance per UIN
  ↓
initWebUI(port=webuiPort)     ← full builds only
```

What the runtime creates:

* **`HookManager`** — discovers QQ main processes and injects the native addon. With `hookAutoLoad: true`, every new PID gets injected automatically.
* **`BridgeManager`** — decodes hook messages from the named pipe into bridge events; caches rkey / contacts / group members.
* **`OneBotManager`** — owns `OneBotInstance`s keyed by UIN; each instance has its own `MessageStore`, `MediaStore`, and `NetworkManager`.
* **`initWebUI`** — full builds boot the WebUI; default port `5099` (override via `runtime.json.webuiPort`).

## Hook + native modules [#hook--native-modules]

The native hook module is loaded via `process.dlopen()`. Source lives in the separate [`dev/nnphook`](https://github.com/SnowLuma/nnphook) repo.

Filename convention:

```text
snowluma-win32-x64.node    snowluma-win32-x64.dll
snowluma-linux-x64.node    snowluma-linux-x64.so
snowluma-linux-arm64.node  snowluma-linux-arm64.so
```

Load search paths:

```text
native/
dist/native/
packages/runtime/native/
```

Native addon API:

* **`getAllMainProcess`** — enumerate QQ main processes.
* **`loadModuleManual`** — manually map the injection module into the target process.
* **`unloadModuleManual`** — unload an injected module.

Default target process is `QQ.exe` on Windows, `qq` on Linux.

## OneBot lifecycle [#onebot-lifecycle]

When the bridge detects a QQ session starting:

1. Load `config/onebot_<uin>.json` (or copy from global if missing).
2. Construct `OneBotInstance`.
3. Boot HTTP / WS / reverse WS / HTTP-POST adapters per `networks.*` config.
4. Asynchronously warm up the friend list, group list, and group members.
5. Forward bridge events into OneBot events.

When the session closes the matching instance is released.

## WebSocket package [#websocket-package]

`@snowluma/websocket` is the in-repo WebSocket implementation; its surface tracks `ws` closely while routing through a native fast path.

Exports:

* **`WebSocket`** — client constructor.
* **`WebSocketServer`** — server constructor.
* **`Server`** — alias for `WebSocketServer`.
* **`InternalWebSocket`** — internal connection implementation.

Loads its own platform-specific `.node` from the same `native/` search paths.

## SDK package [#sdk-package]

`@snowluma/sdk` is a typed OneBot client for downstream consumers — standalone-publishable to npm and independent of the SnowLuma runtime. It's built inside the monorepo (see `pnpm build:sdk` / `build:all` below); for consumer-side usage see the [SDK docs](/en/sdk/).

## Dev scripts [#dev-scripts]

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev              # core dev mode
pnpm dev:web          # WebUI dev server
pnpm build            # core only
pnpm build:webui      # WebUI only
pnpm build:sdk        # SDK only
pnpm build:all        # core + SDK + WebUI
pnpm test             # core tests
pnpm typecheck        # workspace typecheck
pnpm lint             # workspace lint
```

## Build order [#build-order]

Full distribution:

```bash
pnpm build:all
```

Runs, in order:

1. `@snowluma/core` full build
2. `@snowluma/sdk`
3. `webui`

Output goes to the repo root `dist/`.

## Docs site [#docs-site]

The docs site lives in a separate repo: [`SnowLuma/SnowLumaDocs`](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLumaDocs). Local development usually checks it out at `dev/SnowLumaDocs/` alongside SnowLuma.

Stack: Rspress + React + TypeScript + MDX + KaTeX.

The OneBot API reference is generated by the docs repo's `pnpm api:generate` (also wired to `prebuild`) from `docs/public/api/catalog.json` — one page per action, plus a category overview and a searchable landing page. `catalog.json` is the action catalog produced by the main repo's `collectActionDocs()` (same shape as `@snowluma/mcp`'s `CatalogAction`); the main repo's `sync-docs-catalog` workflow commits it here automatically via the SnowLuma bot on release — no manual upkeep.

## Contribution notes [#contribution-notes]

* **Don't bypass `BridgeManager`** — every OneBot action should reach NTQQ through `BridgeInterface`. Keeps the OneBot layer decoupled and testable.
* **Keep configs auto-generatable** — new fields must stay backwards-compatible; normalize them on load and write the result back.
* **Native modules are per-platform** — when adding a platform, sync the `.node` and the injectable library.
* **Tests first** — core OneBot behavior should be validated with `vitest`; see `packages/core/tests/`.
* **API docs automation** — just add the action with `defineAction` (optionally `returnsSchema` to describe `data`); `catalog.json` is kept in sync by the `sync-docs-catalog` workflow, so the API reference never drifts. Run `pnpm api:generate` locally to preview.


---

# Troubleshooting

/en/docs/guide/faq



## noVNC never connects / spins forever [#novnc-never-connects--spins-forever]

* Confirm port `6081` is published. Official templates **do not** publish `5900`.
* There is **no** shared default remote-desktop password. The first start generates a random one and prints it once; later restarts will not print it again — use the value you saved.
* High CPU and no handshake: pass `--ulimit nofile=65536:1048576` (already in official compose).

```bash
docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | grep -E "远程桌面密码:|remote desktop password:" | tail -n 1
```

## Cannot find the WebUI password [#cannot-find-the-webui-password]

The bootstrap password is printed only on the **first start of a fresh data volume**. Reusing a volume will not print a new one.

```bash
docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | grep -E "临时密码|initial credentials" | tail -n 1
```

## A bot cannot reach 3000 / 3001 [#a-bot-cannot-reach-3000--3001]

* In Docker, OneBot should listen on `0.0.0.0`. Upgrading the image rewrites a leftover loopback default; a host you set yourself is left alone.
* On the compose network use the service name `snowluma`, not `127.0.0.1`.
* Send the access token.

## Injection fails / QQ runs but never comes online [#injection-fails--qq-runs-but-never-comes-online]

* You still need `SYS_PTRACE` and `seccomp=unconfined`.
* Do not start a second QQ as root inside the container.
* `ptrace_scope=3` refuses ptrace outright.
* Do not delete the `qq-gateway-data`, `qq-client-config`, or `qq-client-data` volumes.

## Image pull hangs in China [#image-pull-hangs-in-china]

That hop is Docker Hub. The installer retries with prefixes. Manually:

```bash
docker pull docker.1ms.run/motricseven7/snowluma:latest
docker tag docker.1ms.run/motricseven7/snowluma:latest motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

On 1Panel / Baota, set a registry mirror in the panel. The installer will not rewrite `daemon.json`.

## Upgrade asks you to scan again [#upgrade-asks-you-to-scan-again]

Recreating the container can look like a new device. Keep the volumes. If you still must log in again, scan via noVNC.


---

# Introduction

/en/docs/guide/introduction



SnowLuma is a **remote-protocol framework** for NTQQ (the QQ desktop client). It bridges QQ into the [OneBot v11](https://github.com/botuniverse/onebot-11) ecosystem: a native addon injects a hook into the running QQ process via ptrace-class injection (Linux process `qq`, Windows `QQ.exe`), decodes its internal packets, and exposes them as OneBot v11 over HTTP / WebSocket / reverse-WS / HTTP-POST.

Around that core, SnowLuma also ships:

* **OneBot v11 adapters** — HTTP API server, WebSocket server, reverse WebSocket, and HTTP event reporting, in any combination.
* **NTQQ bridge** — talks to the real QQ client directly; no protocol account, no separate login.
* **Multi-account** — one OneBot instance per UIN, auto-detected and auto-attached, no manual config.
* **Built-in WebUI** — manage accounts, config, and status from the browser.
* **TypeScript SDK** — [`@snowluma/sdk`](/en/sdk/), for writing fully typed OneBot clients.
* **MCP server** — [`@snowluma/mcp`](/en/mcp/), so MCP-capable AI clients can query and invoke OneBot actions.

## Three usage shapes [#three-usage-shapes]

| Your goal                         | Shape                    | Start here                                   |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| Run a bot long-term on a server   | **Docker** (recommended) | [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) |
| Let an AI client drive QQ         | **MCP**                  | [MCP integration](/en/mcp/)                  |
| Try it quickly on a local machine | **Prebuilt tarball**     | [Choose a deployment](/en/guide/deploy/)     |

To write client code, see the [TypeScript SDK](/en/sdk/).

## Release layout [#release-layout]

Each platform ships two tarball flavors on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/releases):

| Filename                                                  | Bundles Node.js?            | When to use                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SnowLuma-<TAG>-<platform>-<arch>.tar.gz` (**full**)      | Yes, bundles a Node runtime | No Node installed; runs out of the box                   |
| `SnowLuma-<TAG>-<platform>-<arch>-lite.tar.gz` (**lite**) | No (much smaller)           | Node.js ≥ 22 already installed (Node 24 LTS recommended) |

Published platforms / arches: `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `win-x64`.

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  SnowLuma requires **Node.js ≥ 22**. As of 2026, **Node 24 ("Krypton") is Active LTS** and 22 ("Jod") is Maintenance LTS, so for the lite tarball install **Node 24 LTS** (22 still works). The full tarball bundles its own runtime — no install needed. Source: [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases).
</Callout>

After unpacking, the `dist/` tree looks roughly like:

```text
dist/
├── index.mjs          # entry point: node ./index.mjs
├── launcher.bat       # Windows launcher (node ./index.mjs + pause)
├── webui/             # built-in WebUI static assets
└── native/            # native addon + websocket native modules
    ├── snowluma-win32-x64.{node,dll}
    ├── snowluma-linux-x64.{node,so}
    ├── snowluma-linux-arm64.{node,so}
    └── websocket-<platform>-<arch>.node
```

To run: unpack, then `node ./index.mjs`. On Windows you can also double-click `launcher.bat`.

## Default services [#default-services]

| Service     | Default listen | Notes                                                                             |
| ----------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| OneBot HTTP | `0.0.0.0:3000` | OneBot v11 HTTP API                                                               |
| OneBot WS   | `0.0.0.0:3001` | OneBot v11 WebSocket                                                              |
| WebUI       | `0.0.0.0:5099` | Built-in management UI                                                            |
| VNC         | `5900`         | Docker internal only: native remote desktop. Official templates do not publish it |
| noVNC       | `6081`         | Docker only: browser remote desktop for QR login                                  |

Ports and listen addresses are configurable — see the [Configuration reference](/en/guide/configuration).

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  Do **not** expose noVNC / WebUI / OneBot ports raw on the public internet. Docker has **no** shared default remote-desktop password — the first start generates a random one and prints it once in the container logs.
</Callout>

## Project status [#project-status]

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  SnowLuma is still in **early development**. Interfaces, config structure, and release layout may change between versions. In production, pin a specific version tag and read the [update notes](/en/guide/deploy/update) before upgrading.
</Callout>

## Next steps [#next-steps]

* [Quick Start](/en/guide/quickstart) — not sure where to begin? Start here.
* [Choose a deployment](/en/guide/deploy/) — compare every deployment path and pick one.


---

# Quick Start

/en/docs/guide/quickstart



The first step isn't installing anything — it's **deciding which path to take**. SnowLuma's core injects a hook into a real QQ process, so you need an environment that can run QQ, inject into it, and let you scan a login QR. The table below maps your situation straight to a recommended path — pick the row that matches and follow the link.

## Which path should I take? [#which-path-should-i-take]

| Your situation                     | Recommended path                       | Link                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| A Linux server                     | **Docker** (easiest, recommended)      | [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker)   |
| Windows machine                    | Windows manual / Docker Desktop        | [Windows deployment](/en/guide/deploy/windows) |
| Want to use WSL2                   | Run containers inside WSL2             | [WSL2 deployment](/en/guide/deploy/wsl2)       |
| Only an Android phone              | Termux + proot (advanced/experimental) | [Mobile deployment](/en/guide/deploy/mobile)   |
| Linux server with BT Panel (Baota) | One-click import via Docker App Store  | [BT Panel deployment](/en/guide/deploy/baota)  |
| Hook up an AI client               | MCP server                             | [MCP integration](/en/mcp/)                    |
| Write client code                  | TypeScript SDK                         | [SDK](/en/sdk/)                                |

When in doubt, choose **Docker on Linux** — it's the official, easiest path to a working setup. Full comparison at [Choose a deployment](/en/guide/deploy/).

## Fastest path (Docker) [#fastest-path-docker]

On Linux the recommended path is the official image. Three steps:

**1. Start the container**

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name snowluma \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --shm-size=1g \
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  -p 6081:6081 -p 5099:5099 -p 3000:3000 -p 3001:3001 \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/app/data \
  -v qq-client-config:/app/.config \
  -v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share \
  motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` and `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` are **required**. `--shm-size=1g` is required by QQ. The remote-desktop password is generated on first start and printed once in the logs.
</Callout>

**2. Scan the login QR**

Open `http://<server-ip>:6081/` (noVNC). Password:

```bash
docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | grep -E "远程桌面密码:|remote desktop password:" | tail -n 1
```

QQ is already running on the remote desktop — scan with the QQ mobile app.

**3. Open the WebUI**

Open `http://<server-ip>:5099/`. Full Compose and multi-account notes: [Docker deployment](/docs/guide/deploy/docker).

## Experimental: one-click installer (Alpha) [#experimental-one-click-installer-alpha]

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  **Not the default.** This script is in Alpha and will change. If you already have Docker, use the section above. If you want to help test it:
</Callout>

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh | bash
```

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --mode docker --yes
```

Interactive mode asks which path; `--yes` without `--mode` defaults to docker. Details: [One-click install (experimental)](/docs/guide/deploy/install).

## Login and first access [#login-and-first-access]

Whichever path you take, first-time setup always involves these:

* **QR login**: SnowLuma is **QR-scan login only** — there's no CLI login. On headless setups you must see the QQ window via VNC / noVNC to scan.

* **Find the WebUI temp password**: on the **first** start with a fresh data dir, a one-time admin password is printed to the logs. Docker:

  ```bash
  docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | grep -E "临时密码|initial credentials" | tail -n 1
  ```

  <Callout type="info" title="Info">
    The temp password is printed only on the first start with a fresh data dir. Restarting or reusing an existing data dir will not regenerate it.
  </Callout>

* **Open ports**: to reach it from outside, allow the WebUI (`5099`) and whichever OneBot ports you use (`3000` / `3001`).

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  Do **not** expose noVNC / WebUI / OneBot ports raw on the public internet. There is no shared default remote-desktop password — read it from the container logs.
</Callout>

## Password-free login (URL token) [#password-free-login-url-token]

Tired of typing the password every visit? The WebUI can sign in directly from a **password** carried in the URL:

```
http://<server-ip>:5099/?token=<your WebUI login password>
```

* The query key is `token`, and its **value is your normal WebUI login password**. SnowLuma runs it through the login endpoint; a correct password lands you straight on the home page.
* **Consumed once**: the password is **stripped from the address bar immediately** after load (`history.replaceState`) so it can't leak via browser history / access logs / the Referer header.
* The server still verifies it as usual — a wrong password just drops back to the login page, there's no bypass.

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  Putting a password in a URL is **relatively risky** (it enters browser history and may be recorded by intermediate proxies). Only use it on a trusted local / LAN machine; don't share password links, don't paste them into chats / issues, and don't use them on a shared device.
</Callout>

## Next [#next]

* [Choose a deployment](/en/guide/deploy/) — detailed comparison of every path.
* [Configuration reference](/en/guide/configuration) — ports, access tokens, adapters.
* [Updating](/en/guide/deploy/update) — upgrade without losing your login.

# MCP Usage

/en/docs/mcp



SnowLuma publishes `@snowluma/mcp`, a stdio MCP server. It exposes SnowLuma's OneBot action catalog to MCP-capable clients, so an LLM can look up action docs, parameters, constraints, and JSON Schemas on demand. When you explicitly point it at a running OneBot HTTP endpoint, it can also call actions on a live SnowLuma instance.

Source: [`packages/mcp`](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/tree/main/packages/mcp).

## Modes [#modes]

| Mode    | When it is active                                             | What it can do                                                                                                              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docs`  | Default when `SNOWLUMA_MCP_ENDPOINT` is not set               | Catalog only: action docs, search, categories, and the full catalog resource. It does not contact a live SnowLuma instance. |
| `read`  | Endpoint is set and `SNOWLUMA_MCP_MODE` is not explicitly set | Adds execution for read-only actions such as `get_*` and `can_*`.                                                           |
| `write` | `SNOWLUMA_MCP_MODE=write`                                     | Allows any known action, including side-effecting operations like sending messages or changing group settings.              |

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  Write mode exposes `invoke_action` to your MCP client. Enable it only when you trust the current client, model, and session.
</Callout>

## Requirements [#requirements]

* An MCP client that supports stdio MCP servers, such as Claude Desktop, Cline, or another MCP-capable client.
* The machine running the MCP client needs `npx` and Node.js `>= 22`.
* Docs-only mode does not require SnowLuma to be running.
* Execution mode connects to the **OneBot HTTP endpoint**, not the WebUI port. With Docker defaults this is `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`; the WebUI defaults to `5099` and is only for management.

## Docs-only mode [#docs-only-mode]

You do not need a running SnowLuma instance or a OneBot endpoint. Add this to your MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "snowluma": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@snowluma/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Available tools:

| Tool                          | Notes                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_actions({ category? })` | Lightweight action index, optionally filtered by category.                                                    |
| `get_action({ name })`        | Full docs for one action, including parameter docs, cross-field constraints, return notes, and `inputSchema`. |
| `search_actions({ query })`   | Search by action name, summary, or alias.                                                                     |
| `list_categories()`           | List categories and action counts.                                                                            |

It also exposes the `snowluma://onebot/actions` resource, which contains the full action catalog for the current package version.

## Connect to SnowLuma [#connect-to-snowluma]

To let MCP call real actions, make sure SnowLuma's OneBot HTTP server is reachable. With the default Docker port mapping, an MCP client running on the host usually uses:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:3000/
```

If the MCP client runs elsewhere, replace `127.0.0.1` with the server IP or domain. The HTTP access token is available in the WebUI network adapter settings, or in `config/onebot.json` / `config/onebot_<uin>.json` under `httpServers[].accessToken`.

Read-mode config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "snowluma": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@snowluma/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "SNOWLUMA_MCP_ENDPOINT": "http://127.0.0.1:3000/",
        "SNOWLUMA_MCP_TOKEN": "your-access-token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

This adds one execution tool:

| Tool                                | Notes                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query_action({ action, params? })` | Calls only actions marked read-only and returns the full OneBot response. |

## Enable write mode [#enable-write-mode]

Write mode is explicit:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "snowluma": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@snowluma/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "SNOWLUMA_MCP_ENDPOINT": "http://127.0.0.1:3000/",
        "SNOWLUMA_MCP_TOKEN": "your-access-token",
        "SNOWLUMA_MCP_MODE": "write"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Write mode adds:

| Tool                                 | Notes                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invoke_action({ action, params? })` | Calls any known action, including operations that may send messages, kick users, or change group settings. |

Keep manual approval enabled for `invoke_action` when your MCP client supports approval policies. `query_action` can usually be auto-approved according to your client policy.

## Environment variables [#environment-variables]

| Variable                  | Meaning                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SNOWLUMA_MCP_ENDPOINT`   | OneBot HTTP endpoint, for example `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`. If absent, the server stays in docs-only mode. |
| `SNOWLUMA_MCP_TOKEN`      | OneBot access token. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer ...`.                                                  |
| `SNOWLUMA_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS` | Per-request timeout. Default: `30000` ms.                                                                  |
| `SNOWLUMA_MCP_MODE`       | `docs` / `read` / `write`. Defaults to `read` when an endpoint is set, otherwise `docs`.                   |

## Suggested workflow [#suggested-workflow]

A typical session:

1. Use `search_actions` or `list_actions` to find an action.
2. Use `get_action` to inspect its parameter schema and constraints.
3. Use `query_action` for read-only calls.
4. Switch to write mode and use `invoke_action` only when you deliberately want side effects.

Example prompts:

```text
What parameters does get_group_member_list require?
```

```text
Use SnowLuma to query the current login info.
```

```text
Send "service started" to group 123456, but show me the exact parameters before calling it.
```

## Safety boundaries [#safety-boundaries]

* The MCP server only calls actions present in the generated catalog. Unknown actions are rejected.
* `query_action` accepts only actions explicitly marked read-only.
* `invoke_action` is refused outside write mode, even if a client tries to call it directly.
* OneBot logical failures are returned as response data; only network or transport failures become MCP errors.
* The catalog is a build-time snapshot generated from `@snowluma/onebot`, so it updates with SnowLuma releases.


---

# SDK

/en/docs/sdk



`@snowluma/sdk` is a **fully typed OneBot v11 client** written in TypeScript. It is built for downstream consumers: you don't run SnowLuma in the same process and you don't depend on the SnowLuma runtime — the SDK just connects to any running SnowLuma instance over its OneBot HTTP / WebSocket ports.

The package installs straight from npm and **shares action types with the SnowLuma core**, so call parameters and return shapes can't drift across versions.

<Callout type="info" title="Where the ports come from">
  The SDK connects to the OneBot ports SnowLuma exposes: HTTP at `0.0.0.0:3000` and WebSocket at `0.0.0.0:3001` by default. The `accessToken` also comes from the OneBot config. Make sure those network adapters are enabled first on the [Configuration](/en/guide/configuration) page.
</Callout>

## Install [#install]

<CodeBlockTabs defaultValue="npm" groupId="package-manager">
  <CodeBlockTabsList>
    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="npm">
      npm
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>

    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="pnpm">
      pnpm
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>

    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="yarn">
      yarn
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>

    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="bun">
      bun
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>
  </CodeBlockTabsList>

  <CodeBlockTab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npm install @snowluma/sdk
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>

  <CodeBlockTab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm add @snowluma/sdk
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>

  <CodeBlockTab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn add @snowluma/sdk
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>

  <CodeBlockTab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bun add @snowluma/sdk
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>
</CodeBlockTabs>

Requires **Node.js ≥ 22** (Node 24 LTS recommended). The package is pure ESM (`"type": "module"`) and ships its own type declarations.

## Supported transports [#supported-transports]

| Transport                                  | Client class              | Default endpoint         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| HTTP (POST JSON)                           | `SnowLumaHttpClient`      | `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` |
| WebSocket (forward / reverse, with events) | `SnowLumaWebSocketClient` | `ws://127.0.0.1:3001/`   |

Both clients extend the abstract `SnowLumaApiClient` base, so `call()` / `request()` and every camelCase action shortcut work identically across transports. HTTP suits plain request/response scripts; WebSocket adds **realtime event delivery** on top.

## Constructing a client [#constructing-a-client]

### HTTP [#http]

```ts twoslash
import { SnowLumaHttpClient } from '@snowluma/sdk';

const bot = new SnowLumaHttpClient({
  baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/', // default
  accessToken: process.env.SNOWLUMA_TOKEN,
  requestTimeoutMs: 30_000,          // default 30s
});
```

`SnowLumaHttpClientOptions`:

* `baseUrl?` — OneBot HTTP endpoint, defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`.
* `accessToken?` — token from the OneBot config; when set, an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header is sent automatically.
* `requestTimeoutMs?` — default timeout in ms, defaults to `30000`.
* `fetch?` — custom `fetch` implementation (tests or non-standard runtimes).
* `headers?` — extra headers attached to every request.

### WebSocket [#websocket]

```ts twoslash
import { SnowLumaWebSocketClient } from '@snowluma/sdk';

const bot = new SnowLumaWebSocketClient({
  url: 'ws://127.0.0.1:3001/', // default
  accessToken: process.env.SNOWLUMA_TOKEN,
  reconnect: true,             // enable auto-reconnect
});
```

`SnowLumaWebSocketClientOptions`:

* `url?` — OneBot WebSocket endpoint, defaults to `ws://127.0.0.1:3001/`.
* `accessToken?` — appended to the connection URL as a query parameter.
* `requestTimeoutMs?` — default request timeout, defaults to `30000`.
* `role?` — role the client advertises: `'Api'` | `'Event'` | `'Universal'` (default `'Universal'`).
* `reconnect?` — `true` or a `ReconnectOptions` (`retries` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs`) to enable auto-reconnect after an unexpected close.
* `protocols?` / `webSocket?` — optional subprotocols, optional custom `WebSocket` constructor (Node runtimes or tests).

<Callout type="idea" title="Custom WebSocket on Node">
  Browsers and Node 24 ship a global `WebSocket` that works out of the box. To use an implementation like the `ws` package, pass it to the `webSocket` option.
</Callout>

> The factory functions `createHttpClient(options?)` and `createWebSocketClient(options?)` are equivalent to `new`; use whichever you prefer.

## Calling an action [#calling-an-action]

Common endpoints have fully typed camelCase methods (`getLoginInfo`, `sendGroupMessage`, `setGroupBan`, …). Any registered action can be called via `raw` / `rawResponse`.

```ts twoslash
import { SnowLumaHttpClient, text } from '@snowluma/sdk';

const bot = new SnowLumaHttpClient({ accessToken: process.env.SNOWLUMA_TOKEN });

// Shortcut method
const login = await bot.getLoginInfo();
await bot.sendGroupMessage(123456, text(`Hello from ${login.nickname}`).at('all'));

// Any action: raw() returns data and throws on failure
const fsInfo = await bot.raw('get_group_file_system_info', { group_id: 123456 });

// rawResponse() keeps the full OneBot envelope (status / retcode / data / echo)
const full = await bot.rawResponse('get_status');
```

The underlying methods:

* `call(action, params?, options?)` — sends the action and returns `data`; throws `SnowLumaApiError` when `status` is `failed` or `retcode !== 0`.
* `request(action, params?, options?)` — returns the full response envelope and does not throw on business errors.

Every request can override behavior via `RequestOptions`: `echo` (correlation value), `timeoutMs` (`0` disables the timeout), and `signal` (an `AbortSignal`).

```ts twoslash
import { SnowLumaHttpClient } from '@snowluma/sdk';
const bot = new SnowLumaHttpClient();
// ---cut---
const controller = new AbortController();
const pending = bot.getStatus({ timeoutMs: 5_000, signal: controller.signal });
controller.abort();
await pending; // throws SnowLumaAbortError
```

## Subscribing to events [#subscribing-to-events]

Event subscription is a WebSocket-client capability. The client correlates API responses by `echo` and dispatches packets without an `echo` as events.

```ts twoslash
import { SnowLumaWebSocketClient, text } from '@snowluma/sdk';

const bot = new SnowLumaWebSocketClient({
  accessToken: process.env.SNOWLUMA_TOKEN,
  reconnect: true,
});

// Typed event helpers
bot.onGroupMessage(async (event, ctx) => {
  if (event.raw_message === '/ping') {
    await ctx.reply(text('pong').at(event.user_id));
  }
});

bot.onRequest('friend', async (_event, ctx) => {
  await ctx.approve();
});

// Register a command
bot.command('echo', async (_event, ctx, match) => {
  await ctx.reply(text(match.rest || 'empty'));
});

await bot.connect();
```

Available event helpers: `onMessage` / `onPrivateMessage` / `onGroupMessage` / `onNotice(type?)` / `onRequest(type?)` / `onMetaEvent` / `command()`, plus the lower-level `onEvent`, `when(predicate, handler)`, and `use(middleware)`. Lifecycle events use `on('open' | 'close' | 'error' | 'response' | 'raw', …)`. Every `on` / `when` / `use` returns an unsubscribe function.

The event context (`ctx`) has built-in shortcuts:

* `ctx.reply(message)` — auto-replies to the private/group thread.
* `ctx.approve()` / `ctx.reject(reason)` — handle friend or group requests.
* `ctx.quickOperation(operation)` — calls `.handle_quick_operation`.
* `ctx.stopPropagation()` — stops further middleware dispatch.

## Message builder [#message-builder]

The SDK ships a chainable message builder and segment factories; send methods accept their output directly:

```ts twoslash
import { fromCQString, message, text, toCQString } from '@snowluma/sdk';
// ---cut-start---
import { SnowLumaHttpClient } from '@snowluma/sdk';
const bot = new SnowLumaHttpClient();
// ---cut-end---

// Chained
await bot.sendGroupMessage(123456, text('got it ').at(10001).image('/tmp/a.png'));

// Segment array
await bot.sendGroupMessage(123456, [message.text('Hello'), message.at('all')]);

// CQ-code round-trip
const cq = toCQString([message.reply(42), message.text('hi')]);
const parsed = fromCQString('hi[CQ:at,qq=all]');
```

Built-in segments: `text`, `br`, `face`, `at`, `atAll`, `reply`, `image`, `record`, `video`, `json`, `xml`, `poke`, `forward`, `node`, `share`, `music`, `location`, `contact`, `raw`. `reply()` may appear only once per chain.

## Auto-reconnect, ack correlation, and shared types [#auto-reconnect-ack-correlation-and-shared-types]

* **Ack correlation** — the WebSocket client generates an `echo` per request and routes the response back to the right `Promise`, so concurrent requests never cross. Override the correlation value via `RequestOptions.echo`.
* **Auto-reconnect** — `reconnect: true` (or a `ReconnectOptions`) enables exponential backoff (`minDelayMs` defaults to 1000, `maxDelayMs` to 30000). On disconnect, all pending requests reject with `SnowLumaConnectionError`.
* **Shared action types** — action names, params, and result types share their source with `@snowluma/core`, so the call surface always matches the server.
* **Unified error model** — all errors extend `SnowLumaError`: business failures throw `SnowLumaApiError` (auth-class retcodes become `SnowLumaAuthError`); transport issues throw the `SnowLumaTransportError` subclasses `SnowLumaConnectionError` / `SnowLumaParseError` / `SnowLumaTimeoutError` / `SnowLumaAbortError`.

## Subpath imports [#subpath-imports]

Beyond the main entry, the package exposes per-module exports: `@snowluma/sdk/client`, `/messages`, `/events`, `/types`, `/errors`, `/actions`. Import only what you need.

## See also [#see-also]

* [Configuration](/en/guide/configuration) — enable and secure the OneBot HTTP / WS adapters and get an `accessToken`.
* [Developer guide](/en/guide/developer) — monorepo layout and runtime internals.
* [MCP server](/en/mcp/) — an alternative integration path for LLMs.

# BT Panel Deploy

/en/docs/guide/deploy/baota



<Callout type="idea" title="Community">
  This is a community-contributed and maintained solution. If you encounter issues, please [submit an issue](https://github.com/makotowu/SnowLuma.Docker.Baota/issues).
</Callout>

This page is for "I already run BT Panel, and want to import SnowLuma in one click through the panel's Docker App Store". Under the hood it's the same image as [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) — you just skip writing the Compose file manually.

## Import & Install [#import--install]

1. In BT Panel, go to **Docker → App Store**
2. Switch to the **External Apps** tab and click **Import App**
3. Enter the repository URL: `https://github.com/makotowu/SnowLuma.Docker.Baota`
4. Find **SnowLuma** and click install
5. Fill in the settings:
   * **VNC Password**: if the panel asks for one, set a strong password of your own. Do not reuse a fixed value from old docs or sample posts. The official image has no public default password.
   * **WebUI Port**: default `5099`
   * **noVNC Port**: default `6081`, browser-based remote desktop
   * **OneBot WS Port**: default `3001`, for bot framework integration

Once installed, the container appears in BT Panel's Docker management — logs, start/stop, and editing are all available through the panel UI.

## First Login [#first-login]

After startup, it works exactly the same as standard Docker deployment:

1. Open `http://<server-ip>:6081/` (noVNC) in a browser and enter your VNC password
2. Scan the QR code with your phone's QQ app in the remote desktop
3. The hook automatically switches to working mode after login
4. Open `http://<server-ip>:5099/` to access the SnowLuma WebUI

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  The initial WebUI one-time password is available via `docker logs`. BT Panel's container management UI lets you view logs directly.
</Callout>

## See also [#see-also]

* [Docker (Linux) deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) — full reference for the image, ports, Compose, environment variables, volumes, and multi-account setup
* [Configuration guide](/en/guide/configuration) — customizing ports, access tokens, and adapters
* [Choose a deployment method](/en/guide/deploy/) — detailed comparison of all paths
