# Docker deployment

/en/docs/guide/deploy/docker



On Linux, SnowLuma runs **only via Docker** (host-manual is advanced/unofficial). The image bundles Linux QQ + Xvfb + VNC + noVNC + supervisord + the SnowLuma `lite` distribution, so the host needs nothing beyond Docker.

This page is the **recommended Linux path**. Image build scripts and Compose templates live in [`SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework`](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework). There is also an [experimental one-click installer](/docs/guide/deploy/install) in Alpha — not the default.

## Image [#image]

| Item    | Value                                                               |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Image   | `motricseven7/snowluma:latest` (or a specific tag, e.g. `:v1.10.0`) |
| Arch    | `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`                                        |
| Base    | `node:22-bookworm-slim`                                             |
| Bundled | Linux QQ, Xvfb, VNC, noVNC, supervisord, SnowLuma `lite`            |

The image does **not** rebuild SnowLuma — it consumes the prebuilt `lite` tarball from each SnowLuma GitHub Release, so the release and the image build are decoupled.

## Ports [#ports]

| Port   | Purpose                              |
| ------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `6081` | noVNC (browser desktop for QR login) |
| `5099` | SnowLuma WebUI                       |
| `3000` | OneBot HTTP (default)                |
| `3001` | OneBot WebSocket (default)           |

Official templates **publish `6081` only**. They do not map raw VNC `5900`. Add `-p 127.0.0.1:5900:5900` yourself if you need a native VNC client.

## Remote-desktop password [#remote-desktop-password]

The official image has **no** public fixed password. Do not copy sample values from old docs or random posts.

* **Leave `VNC_PASSWD` unset**: the first start generates a random password and **prints it once** in the container logs (one Chinese line, one English line). It is kept on the data volume. Recreating the container or upgrading the image does not change it, as long as the volume is still there, and it will not be printed again.
* **Set your own password**: pass `VNC_PASSWD` at start. The password is rotated only when you change this value, and the new one is printed once.
* If the variable still holds the old public default from earlier docs, the next start treats it as unset and replaces it with a new random password.

Do not publish `6081` on an untrusted network either.

Read the current password (it only appears when generated or when you rotate it):

```bash
docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | grep -E "远程桌面密码:|remote desktop password:" | tail -n 1
```

If a later restart no longer shows it, that is expected — use the value you saved the first time.

## ptrace permissions [#ptrace-permissions]

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` and `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` are still required.
</Callout>

SnowLuma's native addon uses `ptrace` to inject the hook into the in-container QQ process. The official image grants `cap_sys_ptrace` to `/usr/local/bin/node`, so SnowLuma can run as the unprivileged `snowluma` user while still injecting within the container's capability boundary.

With current official images, you no longer need to change the host's `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope`. Keep these container options instead:

```bash
--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE
--security-opt seccomp=unconfined
```

To verify the file capability inside the container:

```bash
docker exec snowluma getcap /usr/local/bin/node
# expected to include: cap_sys_ptrace=ep
```

If an old image still asks you to relax the host sysctl, upgrade the image first. Changing `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope` should only be a temporary troubleshooting fallback when upgrading is not possible.

## One-line docker run [#one-line-docker-run]

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name snowluma \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --shm-size=1g \
  --ulimit nofile=65536:1048576 \
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  -e SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
  -e SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_PORT=5099 \
  -e SNOWLUMA_QQ_FLAGS="--disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer --disable-gpu-compositing" \
  -p 6081:6081 \
  -p 5099:5099 \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -p 3001:3001 \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/app/data \
  -v qq-client-config:/app/.config \
  -v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share \
  motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` and `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` are **mandatory**. SnowLuma's native addon uses ptrace to inject the hook into the QQ process; the default seccomp profile blocks that.
</Callout>

`--shm-size=1g` is needed for QQ's Chromium runtime — the default container `/dev/shm` is too small and QQ will crash.

## docker-compose [#docker-compose]

Recommended over `docker run`. The repo's `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  snowluma:
    image: ${SNOWLUMA_IMAGE:-motricseven7/snowluma:latest}
    container_name: ${SNOWLUMA_CONTAINER:-snowluma}
    restart: unless-stopped
    shm_size: 1gb
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 1048576
    cap_add:
      - SYS_PTRACE
    security_opt:
      - seccomp=unconfined
    environment:
      VNC_PASSWD: ${VNC_PASSWD:-}
      SNOWLUMA_UID: ${SNOWLUMA_UID:-1000}
      SNOWLUMA_GID: ${SNOWLUMA_GID:-1000}
      SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_HOST: ${SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_HOST:-0.0.0.0}
      SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_PORT: ${SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_PORT:-5099}
      SNOWLUMA_LOG_LEVEL: ${SNOWLUMA_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      SNOWLUMA_SCREEN: ${SNOWLUMA_SCREEN:-1920x1080x24}
      SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD: ${SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD:-1}
      SNOWLUMA_EXTRA_QQ_HOMES: "${SNOWLUMA_EXTRA_QQ_HOMES:-}"
      SNOWLUMA_QQ_FLAGS: "${SNOWLUMA_QQ_FLAGS:---disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer --disable-gpu-compositing}"
    ports:
      - "${NOVNC_PORT:-6081}:6081"
      - "${SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_HOST_PORT:-5099}:${SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_PORT:-5099}"
      - "${ONEBOT_HTTP_PORT:-3000}:3000"
      - "${ONEBOT_WS_PORT:-3001}:3001"
    volumes:
      - qq-gateway-data:/app/data
      - qq-client-config:/app/.config
      - qq-client-data:/app/.local/share

volumes:
  qq-gateway-data:
    name: qq-gateway-data
  qq-client-config:
    name: qq-client-config
  qq-client-data:
    name: qq-client-data
```

Start:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Upgrade:

```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

## Environment variables [#environment-variables]

| Var                        | Default                                                                 | Notes                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `VNC_PASSWD`               | (empty)                                                                 | Remote-desktop password. Leave empty to generate a random one on first start (printed once in the logs). Set it only if you want your own password. |
| `TZ`                       | `Asia/Shanghai`                                                         | Container timezone. Set in Dockerfile, overridable via env.                                                                                         |
| `SNOWLUMA_UID`             | `1000`                                                                  | uid of the in-container `snowluma` user. Match it to the host owner of your mounted volumes.                                                        |
| `SNOWLUMA_GID`             | `1000`                                                                  | gid of the in-container `snowluma` user.                                                                                                            |
| `SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_HOST`      | `0.0.0.0`                                                               | WebUI bind address. Docker examples listen on all container interfaces so published ports work.                                                     |
| `SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_PORT`      | `5099`                                                                  | WebUI listen port (inside the container).                                                                                                           |
| `SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_HOST_PORT` | `5099`                                                                  | WebUI host mapping port (defaults to same as container port).                                                                                       |
| `SNOWLUMA_LOG_LEVEL`       | `info`                                                                  | `error` / `warn` / `info` / `debug`.                                                                                                                |
| `SNOWLUMA_SCREEN`          | `1920x1080x24`                                                          | Xvfb resolution + color depth.                                                                                                                      |
| `SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD`   | `1`                                                                     | Image opts into auto-injection by default. Set `0` to fall back to the manual Load workflow.                                                        |
| `SNOWLUMA_EXTRA_QQ_HOMES`  | empty                                                                   | Comma- or space-separated extra QQ `/app/...` `HOME` paths for auto-starting multiple accounts.                                                     |
| `SNOWLUMA_QQ_FLAGS`        | `--disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer --disable-gpu-compositing` | Flags passed to Linux QQ. The default disables GPU / SwiftShader software rendering to prevent memory leaks.                                        |
| `NOVNC_PORT`               | `6081`                                                                  | noVNC host mapping port. Official templates publish only this remote-desktop port.                                                                  |
| `ONEBOT_HTTP_PORT`         | `3000`                                                                  | OneBot HTTP host mapping port.                                                                                                                      |
| `ONEBOT_WS_PORT`           | `3001`                                                                  | OneBot WebSocket host mapping port.                                                                                                                 |

Environment variables take precedence over `runtime.json`. To restrict the WebUI to the container itself, set `SNOWLUMA_WEBUI_HOST` to `127.0.0.1` and recreate the container.

## Volumes [#volumes]

| Volume             | Container path      | Contents                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qq-gateway-data`  | `/app/data`         | SnowLuma config, cache, SQLite. Includes `config/onebot.json` and `config/runtime.json`. |
| `qq-client-config` | `/app/.config`      | QQ client config.                                                                        |
| `qq-client-data`   | `/app/.local/share` | QQ user data (login state, cache).                                                       |

**Don't delete these on upgrade** — you'll lose login state and configuration.

## First-time login [#first-time-login]

1. Open `http://<host>:6081/` (noVNC) and enter the remote-desktop password from the logs (see **Remote-desktop password**).
2. Inside the remote desktop you'll see QQ already running. Scan the QR to log in.
3. Once login completes the hook auto-switches from passive observation to working mode — no need to click Load in the WebUI.
4. Open `http://<host>:5099/` for the SnowLuma WebUI.

### Finding the WebUI bootstrap password [#finding-the-webui-bootstrap-password]

On a fresh data volume the first launch logs a one-time password:

```bash
docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | grep -E "临时密码|initial credentials" | tail -n 1
```

Just the password string:

```bash
docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | \
  sed -nE 's/.*(临时密码: |initial credentials: user=admin password=)([^[:space:]]+).*/\2/p' | tail -n 1
```

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  The bootstrap password is logged **only on a brand-new data volume's first boot**. Reusing the volume or restarting won't regenerate it.
</Callout>

## Running multiple QQ accounts [#running-multiple-qq-accounts]

Linux QQ ships a single-instance lock — clicking the QQ icon again on a desktop that already has one running just focuses the existing window, it doesn't start a second process. The lock file lives at `$HOME/.config/QQ/SingletonLock`, so the solution is to give each instance its &#x2A;*own `HOME`**.

SnowLuma needs no extra configuration: [HookManager](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/blob/main/packages/core/src/hook/hook-manager.ts) walks every QQ main process it can find, injects the hook into each, and spins up a separate `OneBotInstance` per UIN with its own `config/onebot_<uin>.json`.

### Recommended: auto-start through an environment variable [#recommended-auto-start-through-an-environment-variable]

Mount one dedicated volume per extra account, then list the corresponding container paths in `SNOWLUMA_EXTRA_QQ_HOMES`. The list can be comma- or space-separated:

```yaml
services:
  snowluma:
    # ... existing config ...
    environment:
      SNOWLUMA_EXTRA_QQ_HOMES: /app/qq-acct2,/app/qq-acct3
    volumes:
      - qq-gateway-data:/app/data
      - qq-client-config:/app/.config # primary account
      - qq-client-data:/app/.local/share # primary account
      - qq-client-account-2:/app/qq-acct2 # second account's full HOME
      - qq-client-account-3:/app/qq-acct3 # third account...

volumes:
  qq-gateway-data:
    name: qq-gateway-data
  qq-client-config:
    name: qq-client-config
  qq-client-data:
    name: qq-client-data
  qq-client-account-2:
    name: qq-client-account-2
  qq-client-account-3:
    name: qq-client-account-3
```

On boot, the container generates one supervisor program per extra `HOME`. Each extra QQ runs as the `snowluma` user with the same `DISPLAY=:1` and the same `SNOWLUMA_QQ_FLAGS`, so injection won't fail because a manual `docker exec` accidentally launched QQ as root.

Check process status:

```bash
docker exec snowluma supervisorctl status
# qq, qq-extra-1, qq-extra-2, and snowluma should be RUNNING or starting
```

### Temporarily launch one extra account by hand [#temporarily-launch-one-extra-account-by-hand]

For a one-off launch, keep the user and environment explicit. The important bit is: **do not run the extra QQ as root**.

```bash
docker exec -u snowluma \
  -e DISPLAY=:1 \
  -e HOME=/app/qq-acct2 \
  -d snowluma \
  sh -lc 'qq --no-sandbox ${SNOWLUMA_QQ_FLAGS}'
```

If `/app/qq-acct2` is not mounted to a volume, recreating the container loses that account's login state. For long-term use, prefer the Compose setup above.

### Caveats [#caveats]

* **One HOME per QQ instance** — never share a `HOME` between two QQs; they'll fight over the lock file.
* **Resources**: each QQ is a full Chromium process, \~300-500 MB RAM. The default `--shm-size=1g` is fine for one; bump to `2gb`+ for multi-account.
* **All windows share the same Xvfb desktop**: noVNC shows every QQ window; minimize the ones you've already logged into. Hook keeps working regardless of window state.
* **WebUI lists every UIN automatically**: no manual configuration — SnowLuma surfaces each new account in the WebUI and `get_login_info` returns the new UINs once login completes.
* **Do not rely on desktop autostart folders**: the image uses `fluxbox`, not an XFCE/GNOME session. `~/.config/autostart/*.desktop` may not be read. Let supervisor handle multi-account boot instead.

## Auto-injection [#auto-injection]

The image defaults to `SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD=1`: when the container starts, the hook is injected into the QQ process in passive-observe mode. Once you scan-login, the hook auto-promotes to working mode. supervisor also restarts QQ on crash through the same flow.

### Turning it off [#turning-it-off]

If you prefer the legacy "manual Load via WebUI" workflow:

```bash
docker run -e SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD=0 ... motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

Or set `SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD: 0` in `docker-compose.yml`, or edit `/app/data/config/runtime.json` inside the volume to `"hookAutoLoad": false`. Environment variables win.

## Common ops [#common-ops]

Shell into the container:

```bash
docker exec -it snowluma bash
```

Follow logs:

```bash
docker logs -f snowluma
```

Just SnowLuma's own logs (filter out QQ's noisy output):

```bash
docker logs -f snowluma 2>&1 | grep -v "QtNetwork\|GLib\|libQt6"
```

Browse the data directory:

```bash
docker exec -it snowluma bash -c "cd /app/data && ls -la"
```

Edit OneBot config and restart:

```bash
# edit /app/data/config/onebot_<uin>.json
docker restart snowluma
```

## Port remapping [#port-remapping]

If a host port is taken, just shift the host side; container ports stay the same. Example moving OneBot HTTP to host `8080`:

```yaml
ports:
  - "8080:3000" # host 8080 → container 3000
```

Or via env (the Compose template already supports it):

```bash
ONEBOT_HTTP_PORT=8080 docker compose up -d
```

## Building the image yourself [#building-the-image-yourself]

Useful when you need an unreleased SnowLuma build:

```bash
# Build the lite tarball in the SnowLuma main repo
pnpm build:all

# Drop it into the Docker repo root with the expected name
cp dist/SnowLuma-*-linux-x64-lite.tar.gz \
   ../SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/SnowLuma.Framework.tar.gz

cd ../SnowLuma.Docker.Framework
./scripts/build-image.sh
```

Or let the script pull the latest release:

```bash
SNOWLUMA_TAG=v1.10.0 ./scripts/build-image.sh
```

Multi-arch manifests are merged by CI (`.github/workflows/docker-image.yml`); the local script only builds a single platform.

## Security notes [#security-notes]

* SnowLuma's native addon injects code into the QQ process; the container needs `SYS_PTRACE` and `seccomp=unconfined`. Only run on trusted hosts.
* Do not expose noVNC / WebUI / OneBot ports raw on the public internet. There is no shared default remote-desktop password, but an open port is still enough for someone else to connect.
* Comply with NTQQ / Tencent's terms of service plus SnowLuma's and its dependencies' open-source licenses.


---

# Deployment

/en/docs/guide/deploy



SnowLuma runs in several environments, but the core requirement is always the same: it must be able to run QQ, inject a hook into the QQ process, and let you scan a login QR. Difficulty varies a lot between environments — the table below helps you pick.

Not sure which to choose? See the decision table in [Quick Start](/en/guide/quickstart), or just pick **Docker on Linux**.

## Comparison [#comparison]

| Method                                                      | Platform      | Difficulty | Recommended              | Best for                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Docker](/en/guide/deploy/docker)                           | Linux         | Low        | ✅ **Top pick**           | Long-running on a server, out of the box                         |
| [One-click install](/en/guide/deploy/install)               | Linux         | Low        | ⚠️ Alpha experiment      | One command for Docker / sidecar / host; still in testing        |
| [Windows manual](/en/guide/deploy/windows)                  | Windows       | Medium     | Optional                 | Windows machine, no Docker                                       |
| [Windows · Docker Desktop](/en/guide/deploy/windows-docker) | Windows       | Medium     | Optional                 | Container isolation on Windows                                   |
| [WSL2](/en/guide/deploy/wsl2)                               | Windows + WSL | Medium     | Optional                 | Containers via the Linux subsystem on Windows                    |
| [Linux manual](/en/guide/deploy/linux-manual)               | Linux         | High       | ⚠️ Advanced/unofficial   | Understand the Docker image internals, or no Docker              |
| [Mobile](/en/guide/deploy/mobile)                           | Android       | Very high  | ⚠️ Advanced/experimental | Only an Android phone; resource-heavy, injection may be limited  |
| [BT Panel](/en/guide/deploy/baota)                          | Linux         | Low        | Community                | Already running BT Panel (Baota), one-click via Docker App Store |

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  **Docker on Linux is the recommended, easiest method** — the image bundles QQ + Xvfb + VNC + noVNC + supervisord, so the host only needs Docker.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  **Linux manual** and **mobile** are advanced / unofficial paths: more steps, more pitfalls, and injection may not work in restricted environments (e.g. proot). Unless you know what you're doing, prefer Docker.
</Callout>

## Updating [#updating]

How you upgrade depends on your path, and every path assumes you **keep your login and config**. See [Updating](/en/guide/deploy/update).

## After deploying [#after-deploying]

* [Configuration reference](/en/guide/configuration) — adapters, ports, access tokens.
* [MCP integration](/en/mcp/) / [SDK](/en/sdk/) — hook up an AI client or write code.


---

# One-click install (experimental)

/en/docs/guide/deploy/install



<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  This is an **Alpha** script, **not** the recommended Linux path. Prefer [Docker deployment](/docs/guide/deploy/docker) for real use. The script will change; please try it if you can, and fall back to Docker if it breaks.
</Callout>

One command, no clone. With a TTY it asks for a mode; you can also pass flags.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh | bash
```

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --mode docker --yes
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --mode compose --network maim_bot --yes
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run --mode docker
```

If `raw.githubusercontent.com` is blocked, swap the URL for `https://ghfast.top/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/main/install.sh`. The script lives in [`SnowLuma.Docker.Framework`](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework).

## Modes [#modes]

| Mode      | What it does                                                                       | Who it is for                |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `docker`  | Official image + our compose, QQ bundled                                           | Empty VPS                    |
| `compose` | Sidecar joining an existing Docker network; **does not edit** MaiBot/AstrBot files | You already have a bot stack |
| `host`    | Install QQ + SnowLuma on the host, no Docker                                       | Advanced / **unofficial**    |

There is no joint compose file. The installer will not start MaiBot or AstrBot for you.

## What it handles [#what-it-handles]

* Ubuntu/Debian, Fedora/RHEL/Rocky, OpenCloudOS/openEuler, Arch
* RAM, disk, busy ports, `ptrace_scope`
* China-reachable Docker CE mirrors; **never reinstalls Docker or rewrites `daemon.json` on 1Panel/Baota**
* Image pull fallbacks if Docker Hub is blocked
* No shared default remote-desktop password: if you leave it unset, the first start generates a random one, keeps it on the volume, and prints it once
* Publishes `6081` (browser remote desktop) by default; does **not** publish raw VNC `5900`

## After install [#after-install]

Open `http://<IP>:6081/` to scan the QR code. WebUI is `http://<IP>:5099/`.

```bash
docker logs snowluma 2>&1 | grep -E "远程桌面密码:|remote desktop password:|临时密码|initial credentials" | tail -n 8
```

Full ports, volumes, and multi-account notes: [Docker deployment](/docs/guide/deploy/docker).


---

# Linux (manual, advanced)

/en/docs/guide/deploy/linux-manual



<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  On Linux, **Docker is the recommended and the only officially supported path**: [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) bundles Linux QQ + Xvfb + VNC + noVNC + supervisord + ptrace permissions + hot-update freeze, ready to go. This page **replicates by hand what the image does** — for advanced users who **can't or won't use Docker**. It has many steps and many footguns, and it depends heavily on your distro and kernel settings. If you just want it running, go back to [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker).
</Callout>

This page is the manual version of the official image's `start.sh`: install Node, install Linux QQ, bring up a headless X desktop, grant ptrace to node, freeze QQ's hot-update, run SnowLuma, scan-login. The commands below target &#x2A;*Ubuntu 24.04 (Noble)**; package names and paths differ on other distros — translate accordingly.

## Overview [#overview]

Manual deployment is the same things the image does, in order:

1. Install Node 24 LTS (the lite distribution ships no Node runtime).
2. Install Linux QQ (official `.deb`) plus its Electron / CJK dependencies.
3. Bring up a headless X desktop (Xvfb + fluxbox) + VNC / noVNC so you can scan the QR.
4. Grant `cap_sys_ptrace` to node **without root** (the hook injects via ptrace).
5. Freeze QQ's silent hot-update (black-hole its patch host) to protect the version-pinned native hook.
6. Download and unpack the SnowLuma `-lite` linux tarball, run `node ./index.mjs`.
7. Launch QQ with the documented flags, scan-login via noVNC, open the WebUI.

## 1. Install Node 24 LTS [#1-install-node-24-lts]

SnowLuma needs **Node.js ≥ 22**. In 2026, **Node 24 ("Krypton") is Active LTS** and 22 ("Jod") is in Maintenance LTS — for a fresh install go with 24. The lite distribution has no bundled runtime, so this step is mandatory.

Pick one on Debian/Ubuntu:

<CodeBlockTabs defaultValue="NodeSource">
  <CodeBlockTabsList>
    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="NodeSource">
      NodeSource
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>

    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="nvm">
      nvm
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>
  </CodeBlockTabsList>

  <CodeBlockTab value="NodeSource">
    ```bash
    curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x | sudo -E bash -
    sudo apt-get install -y nodejs
    node -v   # expect v24.x
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>

  <CodeBlockTab value="nvm">
    ```bash
    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.3/install.sh | bash
    # open a new shell, or: source "$HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh"
    nvm install 24
    nvm use 24
    node -v
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>
</CodeBlockTabs>

Node releases: [Node release schedule](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases). With nvm, `setcap` must hit the **real node binary nvm resolved**; redo it after every `nvm install` / `nvm use`.

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  If you downloaded the **full** tarball (which bundles a Node runtime), you can skip this step — but the full package is much larger. This page follows the more common **lite** flow throughout.
</Callout>

## 2. Install Linux QQ and dependencies [#2-install-linux-qq-and-dependencies]

The official Linux QQ download page is JS-rendered, so **don't hard-code a version** — grab the current `.deb` for your arch from [https://im.qq.com/linuxqq/download.html](https://im.qq.com/linuxqq/download.html):

```bash
# Download the current .deb from https://im.qq.com/linuxqq/download.html; substitute the real filename
sudo apt-get install -y ./QQ_*_amd64_*.deb
```

QQ installs to `/opt/QQ/`, with the launcher at `/opt/QQ/qq`.

Install the Electron / CJK runtime deps. &#x2A;*On Ubuntu 24.04 it's `libasound2t64`, not `libasound2`**:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y \
  libgbm1 libnss3 libasound2t64 libgtk-3-0 libxshmfence1 \
  libxdamage1 libdrm2 libxkbcommon0 fontconfig fonts-noto-cjk dbus-x11
```

Without `fonts-noto-cjk`, Chinese text in QQ renders as tofu boxes.

## 3. Headless X desktop + VNC / noVNC [#3-headless-x-desktop--vnc--novnc]

Login is **QR-scan only** — there is no CLI login, so you must be able to *see* the QQ window to scan it. On a headless server, Xvfb provides a virtual screen, fluxbox lets QQ's login dialog map properly, and x11vnc + noVNC project that screen into a browser.

Install (Ubuntu 24.04 package names):

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y xvfb x11vnc novnc websockify dbus-x11 fluxbox
```

Start the virtual screen and set `DISPLAY` (the image uses `:1`):

```bash
Xvfb :1 -screen 0 1920x1080x16 &
export DISPLAY=:1
```

Start a window manager (otherwise the login dialog may be borderless / unfocusable):

```bash
fluxbox &
```

Start VNC (**set a password** — it lands in `~/.vnc/passwd`):

```bash
x11vnc -storepasswd                  # interactively set a VNC password (no weak passwords)
x11vnc -display :1 -rfbauth ~/.vnc/passwd -forever -shared -bg
```

Start noVNC (browser-based VNC, no client needed). On Ubuntu the launcher is at `/usr/share/novnc/utils/novnc_proxy`:

```bash
/usr/share/novnc/utils/novnc_proxy --vnc localhost:5900 --listen 6081 &
```

Then open `http://<your-ip>:6081/vnc.html` in a browser, connect with the VNC password you just set, and you'll see the `:1` virtual desktop.

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  **Never expose VNC (5900) / noVNC (6081) / WebUI (5099) / OneBot (3000, 3001) raw on the public internet.** Bind them to localhost behind a firewall, an SSH tunnel, or an authenticated reverse proxy. Always set a strong VNC password — otherwise your QQ desktop is wide open.
</Callout>

## 4. Grant ptrace to node (without root) [#4-grant-ptrace-to-node-without-root]

SnowLuma's native addon uses `ptrace` to inject the hook into the QQ process. Rather than run as root, give the node binary a file capability:

```bash
sudo setcap cap_sys_ptrace=ep "$(readlink -f "$(which node)")"
```

Verify:

```bash
getcap "$(readlink -f "$(which node)")"
# expected to include: cap_sys_ptrace=ep
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  setcap caveats (read these):

  * **Must be applied to the real binary** — `readlink -f` resolves the symlink behind `which node`; the capability does not follow symlinks.
  * **Dropped on node upgrade / copy** — re-run `setcap` after every Node upgrade.
  * **Needs an xattr-capable filesystem** — `setcap` fails on some overlay / tmpfs mounts.
  * Subject to the kernel's &#x2A;*Yama `ptrace_scope`**: `0` / `1` / `2` all work with the file capability, but `3` disables ptrace entirely. Check with `cat /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope`.
</Callout>

## 5. Freeze QQ's hot-update [#5-freeze-qqs-hot-update]

QQ has a **silent hot-update** channel that quietly rewrites bytes in the background and breaks your version-pinned native hook. (The "Update now" full-package dialog in the UI is click-gated and never fires headless, so you only need to block the silent channel.) Black-hole the patch host:

```bash
echo "0.0.0.0 qqpatch.gtimg.cn" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts
```

Now QQ can't fetch silent patches, the version stays stable, and the hook won't be swapped out from under you.

## 6. Download and run SnowLuma (lite) [#6-download-and-run-snowluma-lite]

Download the &#x2A;*`-lite`** linux tarball for your arch from the GitHub Releases: [https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/releases](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/releases)

```bash
# Pick SnowLuma-<TAG>-linux-x64-lite.tar.gz or -linux-arm64-lite.tar.gz
tar -xzf SnowLuma-<TAG>-linux-x64-lite.tar.gz
cd SnowLuma-<TAG>-linux-x64-lite
node ./index.mjs
```

On first run it creates its config in the data dir (`config/onebot.json`, `config/runtime.json`, etc.) and **logs a one-time WebUI admin password** — note it down, it appears only on a brand-new data dir's first boot.

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  Default services: OneBot HTTP `0.0.0.0:3000`, OneBot WS `0.0.0.0:3001`, WebUI `0.0.0.0:5099`. See [Configuration](/en/guide/configuration) for details. Environment variables override `runtime.json`.
</Callout>

## 7. Launch QQ, scan, open the WebUI [#7-launch-qq-scan-open-the-webui]

Keep SnowLuma running (foreground or another session), then launch QQ under the &#x2A;*same `DISPLAY=:1`** with the documented flags:

```bash
export DISPLAY=:1
/opt/QQ/qq --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer --disable-gpu-compositing &
```

Then:

1. Open `http://<your-ip>:6081/vnc.html`, connect over VNC, and you'll see QQ's QR code.
2. Scan it with QQ on your phone to log in.
3. Once login completes, the hook auto-promotes from passive observation to working mode (`runtime.json.hookAutoLoad` defaults on; set `false` or `SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD=0` to revert to manual Load in the WebUI).
4. Open `http://<your-ip>:5099/` for the WebUI and log in with the bootstrap password from the logs.

Multiple accounts need no extra config: SnowLuma walks every QQ main process, injects each, and spins up one OneBot instance per UIN with its own `config/onebot_<uin>.json`. The key to running more than one is giving each QQ instance its &#x2A;*own `HOME`** (QQ ships a single-instance lock).

## Environment-dependent caveats (be candid) [#environment-dependent-caveats-be-candid]

The manual flow is sensitive to your environment. These bits depend heavily on your machine:

* **Package names / paths** vary by distro (above assumes Ubuntu 24.04). Debian, Arch, and RHEL-family systems differ on `libasound`, the X tools, and the noVNC launcher path.
* **setcap** fails on some containerized / overlay / tmpfs filesystems (see step 4).
* **Yama `ptrace_scope=3`** disables ptrace injection entirely.

If any step gets stuck in your environment, &#x2A;*the easiest path remains [Docker deployment](/docs/guide/deploy/docker)** — the image has already smoothed over all of this.

## 8. Keeping the session alive [#8-keeping-the-session-alive]

When SSH drops, every process you started with `&` (Xvfb / VNC / QQ / SnowLuma) gets `SIGHUP` and dies. Login state lives in QQ's `HOME`; **if the processes are gone, the QR window is gone too**. Long-running hosts need a supervisor.

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  Get the flow working in **tmux** first (QR, WebUI, send a message). Then move to **systemd**. The Docker path does not have this problem: `--restart unless-stopped` already supervises the stack.
</Callout>

All of these processes must share `DISPLAY=:1`, in order: Xvfb, window manager, VNC / noVNC, QQ, SnowLuma.

<CodeBlockTabs defaultValue="tmux">
  <CodeBlockTabsList>
    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="tmux">
      tmux
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>

    <CodeBlockTabsTrigger value="systemd">
      systemd
    </CodeBlockTabsTrigger>
  </CodeBlockTabsList>

  <CodeBlockTab value="tmux">
    ```bash
    sudo apt-get install -y tmux
    tmux new -s snowluma
    # Inside this session, start steps 3, 6, and 7. Do not background them on the SSH shell.
    # Detach: Ctrl-b, then d
    # Return: tmux attach -t snowluma
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>

  <CodeBlockTab value="systemd">
    ```bash
    # Example for a regular user. Adjust the lite unpack path.
    mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
    cat > ~/snowluma-stack.sh <<'EOF'
    #!/bin/bash
    set -euo pipefail
    export DISPLAY=:1
    export HOME="${HOME}"
    Xvfb :1 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -nolisten tcp &
    sleep 1
    fluxbox &
    x11vnc -display :1 -rfbauth "${HOME}/.vnc/passwd" -forever -shared -localhost &
    /usr/share/novnc/utils/novnc_proxy --vnc localhost:5900 --listen 6081 &
    /opt/QQ/qq --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer --disable-gpu-compositing &
    cd "${HOME}/snowluma-lite"
    exec node ./index.mjs
    EOF
    chmod +x ~/snowluma-stack.sh

    cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/snowluma-stack.service <<'EOF'
    [Unit]
    Description=SnowLuma host stack
    After=default.target

    [Service]
    Type=simple
    Environment=DISPLAY=:1
    ExecStart=%h/snowluma-stack.sh
    Restart=always
    RestartSec=5
    LimitNOFILE=65536

    [Install]
    WantedBy=default.target
    EOF

    loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
    systemctl --user daemon-reload
    systemctl --user enable --now snowluma-stack.service
    ```
  </CodeBlockTab>
</CodeBlockTabs>

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  `loginctl enable-linger` keeps the user systemd instance after SSH logout. Logs: `journalctl --user -u snowluma-stack -f`. After editing the script: `systemctl --user restart snowluma-stack`.

  The official host-mode installer splits Xvfb / fluxbox / VNC / noVNC / QQ / SnowLuma into units under `snowluma.target`. Hand-rolling can start with this one wrapper; split later using [`templates/host`](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma.Docker.Framework/tree/main/templates/host).
</Callout>

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  * Do not treat `nohup … &` as a long-running solution: no restart policy, no unified logs.
  * The systemd user unit's `HOME` must be the same one QQ used when you scanned the QR.
  * The `novnc_proxy` path varies; Debian/Ubuntu often uses `/usr/share/novnc/utils/novnc_proxy`.
  * After upgrading Node, run `setcap` again or injection fails on the next restart.
</Callout>

* [Choosing a deployment](/docs/guide/deploy/) — per-platform comparison
* [Docker deployment](/docs/guide/deploy/docker) — the recommended path on Linux
* [One-click install (experimental)](/docs/guide/deploy/install) — Alpha script, including host-mode units
* [Mobile (Android)](/docs/guide/deploy/mobile) — running this manual flow on Android
* [Updating](/en/guide/deploy/update)
* [Configuration](/en/guide/configuration)

# Mobile (Android, experimental)

/en/docs/guide/deploy/mobile



<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  Mobile deployment is **experimental and advanced**, it's resource-heavy, and it isn't for most people. If you have a PC or server, prefer [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker). This page only describes the realistic "it can run" path on Android and is honest about its limits.
</Callout>

## Reality check: Docker barely works on a phone [#reality-check-docker-barely-works-on-a-phone]

Set expectations first:

* **A no-root Linux userland on Android is easy** — install Termux + a Ubuntu via `proot-distro`.
* **But real Docker (dockerd) does not work under proot.** proot is just a ptrace-based syscall emulator; it has no namespaces / cgroups / netfilter, which is exactly what a container runtime depends on.
* Running **real Docker** on a phone requires a VM (QEMU inside Termux, or apps like Podroid). Phones generally have no KVM, so it falls back to TCG software emulation, which is **very slow** and impractical for almost everyone. Google's AVF "Linux Terminal" is a real VM, but its stock image still isn't container-ready as of 2026.

**So the realistic recommendation on mobile: Termux + proot Ubuntu, then run SnowLuma manually following the [Linux (manual)](/en/guide/deploy/linux-manual) flow inside it.** Docker on a phone is for tinkerers and is not recommended here.

For a per-platform comparison see [Choosing a deployment](/en/guide/deploy/).

## Step 1: Install Termux [#step-1-install-termux]

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  **Do not install Termux from Google Play.** The Play Store build is long-abandoned and has known issues. Install from **F-Droid** or Termux's GitHub Releases.
</Callout>

* F-Droid: [https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux/](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux/)
* GitHub: [https://github.com/termux/termux-app/releases](https://github.com/termux/termux-app/releases)

After installing, update first:

```bash
pkg update && pkg upgrade
```

## Step 2: Install a proot Ubuntu [#step-2-install-a-proot-ubuntu]

```bash
pkg install proot-distro
proot-distro install ubuntu
proot-distro login ubuntu
```

Once inside, you're in a Ubuntu userland. Docs: [https://github.com/termux/proot-distro](https://github.com/termux/proot-distro) and [https://wiki.termux.com](https://wiki.termux.com).

## Step 3: Run the Linux-manual flow inside proot Ubuntu [#step-3-run-the-linux-manual-flow-inside-proot-ubuntu]

The rest is **identical** to [Linux (manual)](/en/guide/deploy/linux-manual); do it inside proot Ubuntu:

1. Install Node 24 LTS.
2. Install Linux QQ (`.deb`) plus Electron / CJK deps (note `libasound2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04).
3. Bring up Xvfb + fluxbox + x11vnc + noVNC to scan the QR.
4. Grant `cap_sys_ptrace` to node.
5. Freeze QQ's hot-update (black-hole `qqpatch.gtimg.cn` in `/etc/hosts`).
6. Download and unpack the SnowLuma `-lite` linux tarball, run `node ./index.mjs`.
7. Launch QQ, scan-login, open the WebUI.

Since everything runs on the phone itself, open noVNC / WebUI directly at `http://localhost:6081` / `http://localhost:5099` in the phone's browser.

Follow the full commands in [Linux (manual)](/en/guide/deploy/linux-manual) — they aren't repeated here.

## Honest limitations [#honest-limitations]

* **ptrace injection may be limited under proot.** SnowLuma's hook injects into the QQ process via ptrace, and proot is itself a ptrace emulation layer — whether injection succeeds when the two stack **depends heavily on your device, kernel, and proot version** and is not guaranteed. This is the single biggest unknown of this path.
* **Resource-heavy.** QQ is a Chromium-based Electron app, plus a full Xvfb + VNC + Node stack — heavy on a phone's RAM, heat, and battery. Low-end devices won't cope.
* **arm64.** Phones are almost always arm64 — pick the `arm64` builds of Node, Linux QQ, and SnowLuma.
* **Session persistence.** Termux processes can be killed by the system's battery saver; use Termux's wake-lock and consider disabling battery optimization for the app.
* **Wrong arch won't run.** Use the `linux-arm64-lite` tarball and the arm64 QQ `.deb`.

Overall: &#x2A;*mobile deployment is fine for tinkering or emergencies, but it's not a stable production setup.** For long-term stability, use [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) on a PC or server.

## On "Docker on a phone" [#on-docker-on-a-phone]

If you insist on Docker on a phone, the only viable direction is to run a QEMU Linux VM inside Termux, install real Docker in the VM, and follow [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker). But software-only emulation without KVM is very slow and **not recommended** — noted here for completeness only.

## See also [#see-also]

* [Choosing a deployment](/en/guide/deploy/)
* [Linux (manual)](/en/guide/deploy/linux-manual) — the core steps live here
* [Docker deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) — the genuinely recommended path
* [Configuration](/en/guide/configuration)


---

# Migrate Docker persistent data

/en/docs/guide/deploy/storage-migration



The current image uses a consistent persistent storage layout. Docker does not copy data between named volumes automatically, so an existing deployment must be migrated once when moving from the previous layout.

This procedure preserves SnowLuma and OneBot configuration, the QQ login state, and local QQ data. It does not delete the previous volumes.

<Callout type="error" title="Before you start">
  * Keep the previous container. Do not run `docker compose down` or remove it yet.
  * Never run `docker compose down -v`; it removes Compose-managed volumes.
  * The container must be stopped during the copy, so allow for a short interruption.
  * Keep enough free disk space for the old and new data to coexist during migration.
</Callout>

## 1. Identify the existing container [#1-identify-the-existing-container]

The commands below use the default container name, `snowluma`. Change the first line if you use another name.

```bash
CONTAINER=snowluma
docker inspect "$CONTAINER" >/dev/null
docker inspect "$CONTAINER" \
  --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{printf "%-24s %-8s %s\n" .Destination .Type .Name}}{{end}}'
```

The output must include these container paths:

```text
/app/snowluma-data
/app/.config
/app/.local/share
```

Stop if any path is missing and check the existing deployment configuration.

## 2. Stop the container [#2-stop-the-container]

Stopping the container prevents configuration databases or QQ login data from changing during the copy.

```bash
docker stop "$CONTAINER"
```

Do not remove the container. The copy command reads its existing mounts directly, including volume names generated by Compose.

## 3. Create the current volumes [#3-create-the-current-volumes]

```bash
docker volume create qq-gateway-data
docker volume create qq-client-config
docker volume create qq-client-data
```

Confirm that every destination volume is empty:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/check/gateway \
  -v qq-client-config:/check/config \
  -v qq-client-data:/check/share \
  alpine:3.21 sh -ec '
    for path in /check/gateway /check/config /check/share; do
      [ -z "$(ls -A "$path")" ] || {
        echo "Destination volume is not empty: $path" >&2
        exit 1
      }
    done
  '
```

If this fails, do not overwrite the destination. First determine whether it belongs to an earlier incomplete migration.

## 4. Copy and verify the data [#4-copy-and-verify-the-data]

The following command mounts the previous container data read-only, copies it into the current volumes, and verifies every regular file. It may download the small `alpine` image on first use.

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --volumes-from "${CONTAINER}:ro" \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/migration/gateway \
  -v qq-client-config:/migration/config \
  -v qq-client-data:/migration/share \
  alpine:3.21 sh -ec '
    copy_tree() {
      source_path="$1"
      target_path="$2"
      label="$3"

      [ -d "$source_path" ] || {
        echo "Missing source directory: $source_path" >&2
        exit 1
      }

      (cd "$source_path" && tar -cf - .) |
        (cd "$target_path" && tar -xpf -)

      (cd "$source_path" && find . -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; | sort) > "/tmp/${label}.source"
      (cd "$target_path" && find . -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; | sort) > "/tmp/${label}.target"
      cmp "/tmp/${label}.source" "/tmp/${label}.target"
      echo "Verified: $label"
    }

    copy_tree /app/snowluma-data /migration/gateway gateway
    copy_tree /app/.config /migration/config config
    copy_tree /app/.local/share /migration/share share
  '
```

The command must print:

```text
Verified: gateway
Verified: config
Verified: share
```

If any step fails, stop the migration. The previous data remains in its original volumes.

## 5. Update the Compose configuration [#5-update-the-compose-configuration]

Use the current mounts and explicit volume names:

```yaml
services:
  snowluma:
    volumes:
      - qq-gateway-data:/app/data
      - qq-client-config:/app/.config
      - qq-client-data:/app/.local/share

volumes:
  qq-gateway-data:
    name: qq-gateway-data
  qq-client-config:
    name: qq-client-config
  qq-client-data:
    name: qq-client-data
```

Pull and start the current image:

```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

For a `docker run` deployment, remove the stopped container, recreate it with the same ports and environment, and use these mounts:

```bash
-v qq-gateway-data:/app/data \
-v qq-client-config:/app/.config \
-v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share
```

## 6. Verify the migration [#6-verify-the-migration]

Confirm each item before considering the migration complete:

1. The container remains running without repeated startup errors.
2. The WebUI accepts the existing credentials and shows the previous settings.
3. QQ keeps its login state without requiring another QR login.
4. OneBot listeners, tokens, and bot connections match the previous deployment.
5. A test message can be received and sent successfully.

```bash
docker ps --filter "name=${CONTAINER}"
docker logs --tail 100 "$CONTAINER"
```

<Callout type="idea" title="Keep a rollback path">
  Keep the previous Compose file and volumes until the service has remained healthy through at least one container restart. To roll back, stop the current container, restore the previous Compose file and image version, and start it again.

  This procedure never deletes the previous volumes.
</Callout>

## Bind mounts and multiple accounts [#bind-mounts-and-multiple-accounts]

### Host directories [#host-directories]

If step 1 reports `bind` mounts, the data already lives in host directories and does not need to be copied into named volumes. Keep the host source directory and change only the application-data destination from `/app/snowluma-data` to `/app/data`. The two QQ destinations remain unchanged.

### Multiple accounts [#multiple-accounts]

Additional QQ account destinations remain `/app/qq-acct2`, `/app/qq-acct3`, and so on. To rename those volumes as well, create one new volume per account, repeat the copy and verification process, and keep each account on its own complete `HOME`.


---

# Updating

/en/docs/guide/deploy/update



There's one core rule for upgrading SnowLuma: **replace the program, not the data**. Your login, per-account config, and runtime config all live in the data dir / data volumes — keep them and you won't have to re-scan a QR or reconfigure.

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  The WebUI surfaces an update check, so you can see when a new version is available.
</Callout>

## Docker [#docker]

Easiest. With Compose:

```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

Or pull the image manually and recreate the container:

```bash
docker pull motricseven7/snowluma:latest
docker stop snowluma && docker rm snowluma
# Recreate with the exact same docker run command (volumes unchanged)
```

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  **Do not delete the data volumes** (`qq-gateway-data`, `qq-client-config`, `qq-client-data`). Deleting them loses your login and config. `docker rm` only removes the container, not the volumes — recreate with the same volume names and it picks up right where it left off.
</Callout>

## Manual tarball [#manual-tarball]

1. Download the new release tarball for your platform / arch from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/releases) — same flavor (full or lite) you were using.
2. Replace the program files (`index.mjs`, `webui/`, `native/`, etc.), but **keep your config / data dir** (`config/` and its sibling data).
3. Restart: `node ./index.mjs` (on Windows you can also double-click `launcher.bat`).

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  Keep your data dir outside the unpacked folder, or back it up before upgrading, so you can replace the whole directory without accidentally wiping config.
</Callout>

## Build from source [#build-from-source]

```bash
git pull
pnpm install
pnpm build:all
```

`dist/` is regenerated (`index.mjs`, `launcher.bat`, `webui/`, `native/`). Again, **leave your data dir untouched** and just restart.

## Version pinning and the QQ version [#version-pinning-and-the-qq-version]

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  The bundled QQ version is **pinned** to the native hook. Upgrading SnowLuma itself is safe, but **do not manually update the QQ** inside the container / environment — once QQ's version changes, the version-pinned native hook may break.

  The Docker image already freezes the QQ version by black-holing QQ's silent hot-update host (see [Linux manual deployment](/en/guide/deploy/linux-manual)). On manual / non-Docker setups you should likewise prevent QQ from auto-updating.
</Callout>

In production, pin a specific image / release tag (e.g. `motricseven7/snowluma:v1.10.0`) instead of riding `:latest`, so upgrades are explicit, controlled, and rollback-able.


---

# Windows · Docker Desktop

/en/docs/guide/deploy/windows-docker



<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  **Up front: the SnowLuma Docker image is Linux.** It runs **headless Linux QQ** + Xvfb + VNC + noVNC inside the container. On Windows you run this Linux container through Docker Desktop's **WSL2 backend** — i.e. it's still running inside a lightweight Linux VM.
</Callout>

If you want to run **native Windows QQ** (`QQ.exe`) on Windows, don't use Docker — see [Windows (manual)](/en/guide/deploy/windows) instead. This page is for "I just want a container and don't want to touch native QQ."

Once running, the container is **exactly the same** as in [Docker (Linux) deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) — same image, same `docker run` / Compose, same ports. This page only covers the Windows-side prerequisites.

## Install Docker Desktop [#install-docker-desktop]

Download `Docker Desktop Installer.exe` from [docs.docker.com](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install/) and install it with the **default WSL2 backend**.

### Requirements [#requirements]

* Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11 23H2 and newer
* WSL ≥ 2.1.5
* 8 GB RAM
* Virtualization enabled in BIOS (VT-x / AMD-V), plus SLAT

When you keep the WSL2 backend selected during install (the default), Docker Desktop installs / enables WSL2 for you. Reboot afterward and start Docker Desktop.

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  Confirm you're on the WSL2 backend and not the old Hyper-V backend: Docker Desktop → Settings → General → check **Use the WSL 2 based engine**.
</Callout>

If you'd rather install / manage WSL2 yourself (or run native Docker Engine inside a WSL distro instead of Docker Desktop), see [WSL2](/en/guide/deploy/wsl2).

## Run the SnowLuma container [#run-the-snowluma-container]

With Docker Desktop ready, use the same command from the [canonical Docker page](/en/guide/deploy/docker). Open PowerShell:

```powershell
docker run -d `
  --name snowluma `
  --restart unless-stopped `
  --shm-size=1g `
  --ulimit nofile=65536:1048576 `
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE `
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined `
  -p 6081:6081 `
  -p 5099:5099 `
  -p 3000:3000 `
  -p 3001:3001 `
  -v qq-gateway-data:/app/data `
  -v qq-client-config:/app/.config `
  -v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share `
  motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` and `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` are **still required**. SnowLuma's native addon injects the hook into the container's QQ process via ptrace, which the default seccomp profile blocks. Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend passes these through to the WSL2 kernel, so they work as usual.
</Callout>

The full reference — Compose, environment variables, volumes, multi-account — is **not repeated here**; everything is identical to Linux, so see [Docker (Linux) deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker). Compose works the same from PowerShell:

```powershell
docker compose up -d
```

## Access [#access]

Reach the container's services directly via `localhost` (Docker Desktop forwards the ports to the Windows host):

| URL                      | Purpose                                             |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `http://localhost:6081/` | noVNC — view the remote desktop, scan the QR for QQ |
| `http://localhost:5099/` | SnowLuma WebUI                                      |
| `http://localhost:3000/` | OneBot HTTP                                         |
| `ws://localhost:3001/`   | OneBot WebSocket                                    |

The first-login flow (noVNC QR scan, finding the WebUI temporary password, etc.) is identical to Linux — see [Docker (Linux) deployment · first login](/en/guide/deploy/docker).

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  There is **no** shared default remote-desktop password: the first start generates a random one and prints it once in the container logs. Do not expose noVNC / WebUI / OneBot ports raw on the public internet. Full notes: [Docker deployment · Remote-desktop password](/en/guide/deploy/docker).
</Callout>

## Where to go next [#where-to-go-next]

* [Docker (Linux) deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) — the **full reference** for the image, ports, Compose, env vars, volumes, and multi-account. This page is just the Windows prerequisites.
* [WSL2](/en/guide/deploy/wsl2) — prefer not to use Docker Desktop? Install native Docker Engine inside a WSL distro and run the same container.
* [Windows (manual)](/en/guide/deploy/windows) — to run native Windows QQ (`QQ.exe`) instead of the container's Linux QQ.


---

# Windows (manual)

/en/docs/guide/deploy/windows



On Windows, SnowLuma runs **natively** — no Docker, no WSL2 needed. Install the desktop QQ client, download and unpack the matching SnowLuma release, and run it. SnowLuma discovers `QQ.exe` and injects the hook automatically.

> Want to run it in a container instead? See [Windows · Docker Desktop](/en/guide/deploy/windows-docker) (note: the image is Linux and runs Linux QQ).

## Prerequisites [#prerequisites]

### 1. Install the desktop QQ client (NTQQ) [#1-install-the-desktop-qq-client-ntqq]

Download and install the Windows desktop QQ client (the NT architecture) from Tencent's official site. Make sure `QQ.exe` launches normally. SnowLuma injects into this running NTQQ process.

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  Version matching matters. SnowLuma's native hook is aligned to a specific QQ version. If QQ auto-updates to a newer version SnowLuma doesn't support yet, the hook may fail to load — check the WebUI / README version-compatibility notes if you hit trouble.
</Callout>

### 2. Download a SnowLuma release [#2-download-a-snowluma-release]

Go to [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/SnowLuma/SnowLuma/releases), pick `win-x64`, and choose one of two flavors:

| Package                              | Notes                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SnowLuma-<TAG>-win-x64.tar.gz`      | **Full** — bundles a Node.js runtime, no separate Node install, larger. |
| `SnowLuma-<TAG>-win-x64-lite.tar.gz` | **Lite** — no Node.js, you install Node yourself first, much smaller.   |

Replace `<TAG>` with the version you want (e.g. `v1.10.0`).

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  If you don't want to fuss, grab the **full** package — it ships Node and runs straight out of the box.
</Callout>

### 3. (Lite only) Install Node.js [#3-lite-only-install-nodejs]

SnowLuma needs **Node.js ≥ 22**. As of 2026, **Node 24 ("Krypton") is Active LTS** and 22 ("Jod") is Maintenance LTS. For the lite package, install **Node 24 LTS** (22 still works).

Download the Windows installer from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), then verify in PowerShell:

```powershell
node -v
# should print v24.x.x (or v22.x.x)
```

The full package ships its own runtime — **skip this step**.

## Unpack and run [#unpack-and-run]

Unpack the tarball into a fixed directory, e.g. `C:\SnowLuma\`. After unpacking you'll find `index.mjs`, `launcher.bat`, `webui/`, `native/`, etc.

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  `.tar.gz` can be unpacked with the built-in `tar` (shipped on Win10/11):

  ```powershell
  tar -xzf SnowLuma-<TAG>-win-x64.tar.gz -C C:\SnowLuma
  ```

  7-Zip and similar tools work too.
</Callout>

From the unpacked directory, double-click `launcher.bat` (it just runs `node ./index.mjs` then `pause` so you can read the output). Or run it manually from a terminal:

```powershell
cd C:\SnowLuma
node ./index.mjs
```

If the full package uses its bundled Node, follow the README's launch instructions (usually `launcher.bat` is enough); see WebUI / README for specifics.

## Launch order of QQ and SnowLuma [#launch-order-of-qq-and-snowluma]

SnowLuma has **hook auto-load** on by default: it continuously probes the system for QQ main processes, and when it finds `QQ.exe` it injects the hook automatically (starting in passive observation). After you finish the QR login, the hook switches from passive observation to working mode.

So either order works:

* **QQ first, then SnowLuma**: SnowLuma finds the already-running `QQ.exe` and injects on startup.
* **SnowLuma first, then QQ**: SnowLuma waits until `QQ.exe` appears, then injects.

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  **Run SnowLuma as the same Windows user as QQ.** Injection needs access to the target process; if SnowLuma and QQ run under different users (or mismatched privileges), injection fails. Running one elevated (as administrator) and the other not can also block injection — keep their privileges consistent.
</Callout>

### Login [#login]

Login is **QR-scan only**: scan the QR in the QQ window on your desktop with the QQ mobile app. On native Windows you can see the QQ window directly — no VNC/noVNC needed (that's only for Linux headless setups).

### Disable auto-injection (optional) [#disable-auto-injection-optional]

To keep the traditional "Load from the WebUI" flow, set `hookAutoLoad` to `false` in `runtime.json`, or set the env var `SNOWLUMA_HOOK_AUTOLOAD=0`. Env vars take precedence.

## Accessing the WebUI and OneBot [#accessing-the-webui-and-onebot]

Once running, SnowLuma listens on these ports by default:

| Port   | Purpose                    |
| ------ | -------------------------- |
| `5099` | SnowLuma WebUI             |
| `3000` | OneBot HTTP (default)      |
| `3001` | OneBot WebSocket (default) |

Open the WebUI in a browser:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:5099/
```

### Finding the WebUI temporary password [#finding-the-webui-temporary-password]

On the **first start with a fresh data dir**, a one-time admin password is printed to the console / logs. Scroll through the console window that `launcher.bat` opens (look for the line containing "临时密码 / initial credentials").

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  The temporary password is printed **only on the first start with a fresh data dir** — reusing an existing dir or restarting won't regenerate it. See the WebUI / README for the exact wording.
</Callout>

## Where config lands [#where-config-lands]

The first run auto-creates config files under the data dir:

| File                       | Purpose                                                  |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `config/onebot.json`       | Global default OneBot config.                            |
| `config/onebot_<uin>.json` | One per account (by UIN).                                |
| `config/runtime.json`      | Runtime settings: WebUI port, `hookAutoLoad`, log level… |

Env vars take precedence over `runtime.json`. Multi-account needs no manual config: each UIN you log in spins up its own OneBot instance. Full details in the [Configuration reference](/en/guide/configuration).

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  The exact data-dir location is in the WebUI / README (it can differ by packaging).
</Callout>

## Firewall [#firewall]

On first start, the Windows Firewall may prompt whether to allow `node` / SnowLuma network access.

* For **local-only** access (`127.0.0.1`), you don't need to allow public access.
* To let other devices on your LAN reach the WebUI / OneBot, allow the corresponding ports (`5099` / `3000` / `3001`) through the firewall.

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  **Never expose the WebUI / OneBot ports raw on the public internet.** These ports give full control over your QQ. For remote access, go through a reverse proxy with auth or an authenticated tunnel, and change the default credentials.
</Callout>

## Next steps [#next-steps]

* [Configuration reference](/en/guide/configuration) — OneBot / runtime options explained.
* [Quickstart](/en/guide/quickstart) — connect your first OneBot client.
* [MCP](/en/mcp/) / [SDK](/en/sdk/) — building on top of SnowLuma.
* Other platforms: [Docker (Linux)](/en/guide/deploy/docker), [WSL2](/en/guide/deploy/wsl2), [deployment overview](/en/guide/deploy/).


---

# WSL2

/en/docs/guide/deploy/wsl2



WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux 2) gives you a real Linux kernel on Windows. Running SnowLuma's Linux container inside it is the alternative route when you don't want native Windows QQ.

This page covers: install WSL2, get Docker running one of two ways, then start the [canonical SnowLuma container](/en/guide/deploy/docker).

<Callout type="idea" title="Tip">
  If you already use / plan to use **Docker Desktop**, it ships WSL2 integration and is simpler — see [Windows · Docker Desktop](/en/guide/deploy/windows-docker). This page is for people who want to install **Docker Engine themselves** inside a WSL distro, or who prefer working closer to Linux.
</Callout>

## 1. Install WSL2 [#1-install-wsl2]

Open PowerShell **as administrator** and run:

```powershell
wsl --install
```

This installs WSL2 plus the default Ubuntu distro. **Reboot**; on reboot Ubuntu starts for the first time and asks you to create a Linux username and password.

Confirm the version is 2:

```powershell
wsl -l -v
# the VERSION column should read 2
wsl --set-default-version 2
```

Current Ubuntu-on-WSL ships with systemd enabled.

> Official docs: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install)

## 2. Get Docker into WSL2 (pick one — don't do both) [#2-get-docker-into-wsl2-pick-one--dont-do-both]

### Route A: Docker Desktop's WSL integration (recommended) [#route-a-docker-desktops-wsl-integration-recommended]

After installing Docker Desktop, go to Settings → Resources → WSL Integration and enable integration for your Ubuntu distro. Then the `docker` command works directly in the Ubuntu terminal, with the engine running on the Docker Desktop side. For install and system requirements, see [Windows · Docker Desktop](/en/guide/deploy/windows-docker).

> Official docs: [https://docs.docker.com/desktop/features/wsl/](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/features/wsl/)

### Route B: Native Docker Engine inside the distro [#route-b-native-docker-engine-inside-the-distro]

If you'd rather not install Docker Desktop, install native Docker Engine directly inside the Ubuntu distro. For the official apt repo (deb822 `docker.sources` format), see [https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/).

For local / dev use only, the convenience script also works:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
```

After adding yourself to the group you must **reopen the terminal** for it to take effect. Start Docker:

```bash
# distros with systemd enabled:
sudo systemctl start docker
sudo systemctl enable docker

# older setups without systemd:
sudo service docker start
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  **Pick Route A or B — don't run both.** Docker Desktop's integration and a native dockerd inside the distro will fight each other if both are present.
</Callout>

## 3. Run the SnowLuma container [#3-run-the-snowluma-container]

With Docker ready, run the exact same command from the [canonical Docker page](/en/guide/deploy/docker) in the Ubuntu terminal:

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name snowluma \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --shm-size=1g \
  --ulimit nofile=65536:1048576 \
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  -p 6081:6081 \
  -p 5099:5099 \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -p 3001:3001 \
  -v qq-gateway-data:/app/data \
  -v qq-client-config:/app/.config \
  -v qq-client-data:/app/.local/share \
  motricseven7/snowluma:latest
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Warning">
  `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE` and `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` are **required** — the hook injects via ptrace, which the default seccomp profile blocks.
</Callout>

The full reference — Compose, env vars, volumes, multi-account, first login — all lives in [Docker (Linux) deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) and is not repeated here.

## 4. Accessing ports from Windows [#4-accessing-ports-from-windows]

WSL2 forwards container-listened ports to the Windows `localhost` by default, so you can use `localhost` directly in a Windows browser:

| URL                      | Purpose                |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------- |
| `http://localhost:6081/` | noVNC (scan QR for QQ) |
| `http://localhost:5099/` | SnowLuma WebUI         |
| `http://localhost:3000/` | OneBot HTTP            |
| `ws://localhost:3001/`   | OneBot WebSocket       |

<Callout type="info" title="Info">
  In rare setups `localhost` forwarding may not work (disabled, or a different networking mode). In that case get the WSL IP with `wsl hostname -I` and use that IP instead.
</Callout>

<Callout type="error" title="Danger">
  There is **no** shared default remote-desktop password: the first start generates a random one and prints it once in the container logs. Do not expose noVNC / WebUI / OneBot ports raw on the public internet. Full notes: [Docker deployment · Remote-desktop password](/en/guide/deploy/docker).
</Callout>

## Alternatively: the Linux-manual flow inside WSL2 [#alternatively-the-linux-manual-flow-inside-wsl2]

WSL2 is, after all, a Linux environment, so in principle you could run SnowLuma the Linux-manual way without Docker (bring up Xvfb / VNC / noVNC yourself, install linuxqq, grant node the ptrace capability, etc.). But that's clearly more involved — **Docker is simpler** — so this page recommends the container route.

## Where to go next [#where-to-go-next]

* [Docker (Linux) deployment](/en/guide/deploy/docker) — the full container reference.
* [Windows · Docker Desktop](/en/guide/deploy/windows-docker) — use Docker Desktop instead of an in-distro Engine.
* [Windows (manual)](/en/guide/deploy/windows) — to run native Windows QQ instead of the container's Linux QQ.
